ElevenLabs is in early talks to raise at a $33B valuation, Bloomberg says

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that elevenLabs is in early talks for a funding round at a $33B valuation, planned for the first quarter of 2027, Bloomberg reported.
  • According to recent reports, elevenLabs is in early talks to raise money at a $33B valuation, Bloomberg reported on Wednesday, citing people familiar with the matter.
  • Sources indicate that that would be a 50% jump from the $22B ElevenLabs was valued at in a $300M share sale in September.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that elevenLabs is in early talks for a funding round at a $33B valuation, planned for the first quarter of 2027, Bloomberg reported. That would be 50% above its $22B valuation in September, and its annual recurring revenue has reached $700M, one person remarked.

According to recent reports, elevenLabs is in early talks to raise money at a $33B valuation, Bloomberg reported on Wednesday, citing people familiar with the matter. The voice AI company looks to start the round in the first quarter of 2027, though some investors want it to begin sooner.

Sources indicate that that would be a 50% jump from the $22B ElevenLabs was valued at in a $300M share sale in September. It also fits the company’s habit of setting valuations in multiples of 11, a nod to its name.

According to recent reports, elevenLabs’ annual recurring revenue has reached $700M, one person told Bloomberg, up from the $600M it reported in September. ElevenLabs declined to comment.

According to recent reports, the price would be steep next to its peers. London video AI firm Synthesia was valued at $4B in January with about $140M in yearly revenue. Mistral was valued at €21B in September, having passed $400M early in the year.

Investors may be spurred on by Anthropic’s record $107.3B IPO, which brought early backers huge gains.

According to recent reports, elevenLabs was founded in London in 2022 by Mati Staniszewski and Piotr Dabkowski, and makes realistic AI voices for games, audiobooks and AI agents. Staniszewski has remarked it could start preparing for an IPO in 2028.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that iOS 27 brought latest features to Apple Wallet, Maps, Notes, Messages, and more—and it includes key upgrades for the Mail app too. Here’s everything new for Apple Mail in iOS 27.

If you have much history using Apple Mail, you’ll know that its search feature hasn’t always been the best. But in iOS 27, search has gotten a massive upgrade.

More relevant search in Mail. A fresh ranking system brings the most relevant results to the top to help you find what you need right away — even if it’s buried deep in your inbox.

It has been revealed that I can’t count the number of times search has previously failed to find messages that I knew existed. So far in my usage, iOS 27 has fixed that.

According to recent reports, suggestions at the top of messages have been in Apple Mail for years. But in iOS 27, they have a latest, more flexible design and expand to support third-party apps.

When Mail detects that you might want to take action on the contents of an email, a suggestion might appear at the top of the message. These include: directions in Maps, creating events in Calendar, tracking a shipment with Apple Wallet, and more.

It has been revealed that in iOS 27, third-party apps can offer suggestions too. And when multiple apps are available with suggested actions, there’s a drop-down menu to show you all available options.

Smart Reply is a keyboard feature that automatically surfaces reply options you can utilize with a single tap.

In iOS 27, the next generation of Apple Intelligence comes with improvements to Smart Reply.

Apple states that Smart Reply “can now draw on a user’s personalized writing style.” Essentially, rather than offering fairly generic reply options, now Smart Reply suggestions will actually sound a lot more like you.

In a recent development, apple has added ‘Ask Siri’ buttons throughout Apple Mail, just like the rest of its system apps. And Siri AI brings a bunch of upcoming powers for Mail users.

One example I’ve seen several times on social media is that you can ask Siri to delete all messages from a specific sender that’s spamming you.

I asked the fresh Siri on iOS 27 to delete Spam emails from a particular adddess and it just did that so seamlessly pic.twitter.com/EYn74buYAX.

Beyond new features, Apple also claims that iOS 27 makes the Mail app run better than ever thanks to bug fixes and performance improvements. Here are some specific examples given:.

Perplexity’s Time Machine lets AI agents search the web of the past

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (343 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Thenextweb

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, perplexity has added Time Machine to its Search and Context APIs, letting agents see the web as it was up to 365 days ago so forecasting tests are not spoiled by hindsight.
  • According to recent reports, perplexity has rolled out Time Machine, a tool that lets AI agents search the web as it looked on a past date, the manufacturer said on Wednesday.
  • Industry observers note that both target the same problem.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Perplexity’s artwork for its Time Machine API.

In a recent development, perplexity has added Time Machine to its Search and Context APIs, letting agents see the web as it was up to 365 days ago so forecasting tests are not spoiled by hindsight. It follows Epochal’s Time Portal by a day, and Perplexity’s results come from its own tests.

According to recent reports, perplexity has rolled out Time Machine, a tool that lets AI agents search the web as it looked on a past date, the manufacturer said on Wednesday. It arrived a day after Epochal, a startup from three of xAI’s co-founders, launched a similar product.

Industry observers note that both target the same problem. An AI agent asked about a past election or earnings call can simply look up the result. That makes it hard to test how well it really predicts.

Time Machine adds a date cutoff to Perplexity’s search and page-reading tools for developers, so results come from copies saved before that date. Perplexity’s cutoffs reach back 365 days. Epochal indicates its archive spans more than 30 years.

Recent findings suggest that perplexity notes it used the tool to train an AI model to forecast 2026 political events listed on Polymarket. In its own test, the trained model scored 0.80, just above the market’s 0.79.

In a recent development, it also notes fewer of its pages leaked later information than rival Exa’s, at 0.25% against 1.10% in one test. That was judged by Perplexity’s own automated checker. Time Machine costs the same as Perplexity’s other API calls.

Web tools built for AI agents are multiplying. On the same day, Cloudflare began letting websites offer agents their own search.

Archives of the web are becoming contested ground. More than 241 news outlets now block the Wayback Machine to keep AI companies away from their old articles.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, back in July, PrismML claimed its roughly 4 GB, 1-bit Bonsai 27B was the first AI model of its size to run on an iPhone.
  • The startup also drew attention when CEO Babak Hassibi told CNBC that Apple was evaluating its technology, as we reported at the time.
  • In a recent development, the new model is based on Qwen3.8 27B and keeps the same 5.9 GB footprint in its most compact format.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, back in July, PrismML claimed its roughly 4 GB, 1-bit Bonsai 27B was the first AI model of its size to run on an iPhone. Now PrismML has released Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B, an upgrade to the model it introduced in September.

The startup also drew attention when CEO Babak Hassibi told CNBC that Apple was evaluating its technology, as we reported at the time.

In a recent development, the new model is based on Qwen3.8 27B and keeps the same 5.9 GB footprint in its most compact format. This time, PrismML focused on helping the model handle longer tasks, including figuring out what to do when a tool returns an unexpected result or a step fails.

Sources indicate that bonsai 2.5 improved on six of the seven benchmarks PrismML highlights. Its SWE-bench Verified coding score rose from 60.8 to 75.6, while its AppWorld tool-use score jumped from 51.2 to 90.5. LiveCodeBench v6 dipped from 83.8 to 83.0.

What could that look like on a Mac? A coding assistant could inspect a private project, make a change, run the tests, and use the results to revise its fix. A document app could summarize a folder of sensitive files while keeping the processing on the device.

PrismML says Bonsai 2.5 runs on Mac, iPhone, and iPad through MLX. Its Apple silicon package is about 8.9 GB, and the model card walks through setup on a Mac. The weights are available for free under Apache 2.0.

For a closer look at how the model was compressed and tested, read PrismML’s technical white paper.

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Vox ↗ Open Full Page

A few questions for the guy who went snorkeling in a Home Depot retention pond

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2015 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vox

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • One night earlier this fall, a biologist and YouTuber in Florida named Joseph Ricketts went snorkeling in a retention pond next to his local Home Depot.
  • He filmed what he saw and posted a video to his channel titled “Night Snorkel In a Home Depot Retention Pond.” It swiftly blew up, hitting more than 2 million views as of this writing, and for good reason: It’s not at all what you might expect.
  • Recent findings suggest that ricketts found an aquatic world teeming with life on his dive into what is, from the surface, a stagnant pool of water filled with old beer cans.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

He found it teeming with life and beauty.

One night earlier this fall, a biologist and YouTuber in Florida named Joseph Ricketts went snorkeling in a retention pond next to his local Home Depot.

He filmed what he saw and posted a video to his channel titled “Night Snorkel In a Home Depot Retention Pond.” It swiftly blew up, hitting more than 2 million views as of this writing, and for good reason: It’s not at all what you might expect.

Recent findings suggest that ricketts found an aquatic world teeming with life on his dive into what is, from the surface, a stagnant pool of water filled with old beer cans. A water snake undulated through the pond, a bulge in its stomach revealing a recent meal. Tadpoles darted about, some of them half on their way to froghood. Mysterious shrimp scuttled along the silty bottom.

Ricketts, who works as a crocodile and alligator research biologist in Florida, went for his first snorkeling trip when he was 16 years old. On that trip, he came face-to-face with a manatee — and was instantly hooked. “I experienced so much joy in that moment, and I just kind of subconsciously knew I’d be chasing that for the rest of my life to some degree or another,” he told me.

Ricketts still takes a lot of joy in snorkeling, in part because of how it allows him to promptly access a totally different world hiding just under the surface of the water; his YouTube bio declares, “I’ll snorkel pretty much anywhere.” And his recent retention pond dive among the suburban detritus bears that out.

Industry observers note that I talked with Ricketts recently about urban ecology, snorkeling, and what motivates a person to jump into the pond behind the Home Depot three miles from his house (his shortest-ever commute to a dive yet). Our interview has been edited for length and clarity.

That’s a good question. I’m scuba certified, and I enjoy anything underwater, but snorkeling is just super accessible. I have a camera housing and a wet suit and other gear, but really all you need is just a mask and snorkel. As long as the water’s not freezing cold, you can get in there and take a look around. I really enjoy how, as soon as you immerse your head, it feels like you’re in a totally different world.

But the beautiful thing is that you’re not. You’re in the same world, it’s just this is the one that you didn’t have a vision into before. It’s kind of a meditative, calming practice. Just taking a look around at what is happening in nature and how things survive in their own environment is pretty awesome. I love it.

It has been revealed that I honestly had the idea for it a couple years ago. I’d see people out there birding with binoculars and telephoto lenses, and I started wondering if I could snorkel in there. We’ve had a drought so I couldn’t do it for a really long time, and when we finally got some rain I decided to go for it.

According to recent reports, tell me about the retention pond. What is it — and why is it in this Home Depot parking lot?

Florida has a lot of low-level, very wet natural ecosystems, but it’s also an extremely developed state. There are strip malls and roads and concrete everywhere! Natural wetland environments can soak up intense stormwater, but when you totally change environments and put in shopping centers and neighborhoods and pave everything with asphalt, you kind of lose that ability. That stormwater needs a place to go and collect — or it’s just going to flood parking lots and stores and houses.

So they have to put these retention ponds in; nowadays, you can’t build in certain areas unless you put in a retention pond. Not far from the Home Depot is a latest-build neighborhood, and they have a retention pond that they had to put in, but they set it up with a little walkway for people that live in the neighborhood. That’s nice because there’s some wildlife that’s able to survive and live there, and people can enjoy this sort-of natural area. But it’s also not as good as the original thing that may have been there, you know?

So you were snorkeling in what’s essentially a replacement for a wetland that might once have been there.

I don’t know the history of that area exactly, but I imagine there was some form of wetland.

What was the most surprising thing that you found?

One thing that I found was a tadpole shrimp, which people call triops. It’s a freshwater crustacean that apparently is not native to Florida. When I saw it underwater, I had no context for what it is. As a biologist, people assume you just know wildlife, but people forget how much wildlife there is in the world! I know a lot about alligators and crocodiles, but there’s still a ton I don’t know. I think it’s important to sometimes be able to be like: “I don’t know what I’m seeing or why I’m seeing it” — and then hopefully I can learn about it.

It has been revealed that but anyway, I saw this thing, I had no clue what it was, and I asked a bunch of my coworkers about it but they had no clue what it was either. So then I had to do some research online, which is how I finally figured it out.

“I think that was kind of a personal challenge I had for myself: Can I see something beautiful in a retention pond?”.

Apparently they are native to the Midwest. They lay their eggs in soil, and then during times of rain, they really quickly hatch and feed and grow, and then they reproduce, lay more eggs, and then wait for the next cycle while it’s dry. It’s a real quick boom-and-bust life cycle. It’s not a native species, but I think there’s just a couple areas in this state where you can find them — and one just happens to be right there in the retention pond.

I saw that there were also more common animals there, like frogs, snakes, and dragonflies. But how do you think they all got into this parking-lot pond?

A lot of frog species adapt to urban environments and find any bit of water they can. They were probably used to a forest and wetland, and now they’ve had to adapt to what’s available presently, which is pretty limited.

According to recent reports, I think that’s true for most of the animals you find in there. The natural world is pretty resilient, though sometimes I think we give it too much credit for how resilient it can be.

Life survives, but the way things originally were does not necessarily survive, and I think that’s something that’s really worth protecting. The way some people interpreted the video was like: ”Wow, look at all this life persisting even in this place!” And it was amazing and there is beauty there, but you can’t just accept that and then get rid of all our natural wetlands. We need untouched, expansive ecosystems.

It has been revealed that it can be cool to be excited about this little retention pond and what lives in here, but coupled with that also needs to be excitement for protecting huge untouched habitat as well. Both are full of worthy things.

Do you think the retention pond, now that it’s there, is worth preserving?

Industry observers note that I think so. One thing I didn’t really get to dive into with the video too much is the idea of a nature desert. I don’t know if I’m making that term up, but it’s kind of related like a food desert: Depending on your demographic or where you’re born, that might be the only bit of nature you have access to. It’s a privilege to be able to travel to a national park or a substantial state park or something, and not everyone has that opportunity. Your only exposure to nature could be a retention pond that’s in the middle of a city somewhere. And so I do think those places are very worth protecting, because I think it’s crucial that regardless of your background, if you’re a kid, you have a place that you can go to and feel safe and be exposed to wilderness even if it’s very small urban wilderness.

Do you think people should be snorkeling in more retention ponds?

In a recent development, [Laughs] I don’t recommend that people do that! There are some retention ponds where you could encounter some nasty stuff.

Industry observers note that it was definitely a little bit of a stunt. But I also want to help people think about ecological ideas that they might not otherwise think of, while still enjoying the watch.

Another thing I want to get at is so many people responded like: “That’s gross, how could you do that?” But my question is why are we just totally okay with having these huge bodies of water that are gross and contaminated in our everyday lives? Clean water should be the norm!

Still, it’s a place that should be valued and thought of differently.

Do you feel like your own perception of urban ecology or urban environments changed after this?

I think so. That’s another reason why I love snorkeling: I feel like somehow each time I do it, it changes me a little bit. I didn’t know that much life was out there, and I didn’t know what a lot of those creatures were when I first got in. It deepens my personal connection with my local Home Depot in a way I hadn’t really thought would happen five years ago, but here we are.

Do you think you’ll do more urban snorkeling? I know you just went to the Dry Tortugas, which is a very different environment from Home Depot.

It has been revealed that I think I am going to look into it. I’m not going to become the retention pond snorkeling guy; I hope to diversify my snorkeling more than that. But I definitely think this is an idea that resonates with people, and it gives me an opportunity to explore some interesting ecological and even philosophical concepts.

Sources indicate that I’ve got some other ideas that I’ve been waiting for the right time to film. There’s a place up in the Carolinas that’s a Frisbee golf course with a little creek running through it, and there are these amazing minnow spawning events that happen in the creek, so maybe one day I’ll be out there in the creek filming minnow spawning while people are playing Frisbee golf nearby.

What are you hoping people take away from the video?

One thing that I hope people take away from a lot of my videos is just a sense of wonder at what’s out there in the natural world, and maybe a broader definition of beauty. I think beauty can be found in unexpected places and from unexpected creatures. I think that was kind of a personal challenge I had for myself: Can I see something beautiful in a retention pond? And do I have the skill with my camera to present that so that maybe other people catch a little glimmer of it too? And I think it happened, which is really exciting.

But at the same time, I hope people realize how important it is that big expansive habitats are protected and conserved too, and that it’s not just about the big animals like polar bears and manatees, which are kind of easy to care about, but also little rare invertebrates or spiders or snakes, all of which I believe have inherent value and are worth protecting.

An annoying ‘mistake’ in macOS was actually prep for the latest MacBook Pro

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (472 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: 9to5mac

💡 Key Takeaways
  • You may remember that Apple made a seeming mistake in the user interface for macOS 26, meaning that attempts to resize windows would often fail.
  • I was one of a number of people to note that trying to grab the corner of a window in macOS Tahoe in order to resize it would often fail.
  • It turns out that my initial click in the window corner instinctively happens in an area where the window doesn’t respond to it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You may remember that Apple made a seeming mistake in the user interface for macOS 26, meaning that attempts to resize windows would often fail. The reason for this has now become clear, and Apple has done something both fun and clever in macOS 27 to resolve it ….

I was one of a number of people to note that trying to grab the corner of a window in macOS Tahoe in order to resize it would often fail. Developer Norbert Heger pointed out this is because Apple changed the radius of the corners without changing the grabbable area.

It turns out that my initial click in the window corner instinctively happens in an area where the window doesn’t respond to it. The window expects this click to happen in an area of 19 × 19 pixels, located near the window corner. If the window had no rounded corners at all, 62% of that area would lie inside the window. But due to the huge corner radius in Tahoe, most of it – about 75% – now lies outside the window.

At the time, the radius change itself looked like an inexplicable mistake on Apple’s part, and the company did revert it. However, Macworld’s Michael Simon appears to have discovered the reason for the original change.

The latest rounder corners on the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR are basically a perfect match for the macOS 26 radii.

So if you move a window to the corner of the upcoming machine, it would fit perfectly. However, since Apple reverted the corner radius, it would no longer do so. The company solved this by a clever UI transition.

What’s happening there is Golden Gate’s 20-point corner radius is subtly and gradually expanding when It approaches the bottom corner of the screen to match the exact corner of the display, which is much larger. I can’t be certain it’s exactly 26-point, but it sure looks like it to me. The effect is incredible. I’ve watched it like 20 times and I can barely see it changing, yet when it reaches the corner it’s perfectly expanded to match.

Recent findings suggest that you can see this illustrated by a GIF in the Macworld piece. While the original change annoyed me, Apple’s solution is the perfect example of the company sweating the details.

Code Red is a common term used to describe the highest priority response to a major problem, pulling a significant number of engineers off their current tasks in order to maximize the resources applied to fixing it.

The senior execs responsible for the service told staff that it was the most customer-impacting incident ever experienced, and has acknowledged that not only was the problem itself unacceptable, but so too was the time taken to resolve it. Reuters got sight of a memo sent to the team.

In a recent development, it was the most ⁠customer-impacting incident in the history of Exchange Online, M365 Core President Jason Henderson said in a memo to staff on Friday. Never before had so many customers been without email for so long, he said. “Code Red means that this is the highest priority work for our team,” Henderson added.

Charles Lamanna, Microsoft’s executive vice president of Copilot, Agents and Platform, told a Code Red review that the affected component had experienced “roughly ten years’ worth of acceptable failures,” according to Silver’s memo.

One reason it took so long to work out what had happened was because the diagnostic data needed was “scattered across fragmented internal systems.” The memo indicates 11 separate Teams chats exchanged more than 11,000 messages as they struggled to work out what exactly had gone wrong.

Microsoft is now working on five interrelated approaches to achieve a target resolution time of less than an hour for any future incidents of this nature.

Recent findings suggest that AI-powered workspaces are tech companies’ latest focus, as the industry still struggles to perfect adoption. Microsoft has just put its offering into the ring.

During the keynote for the manufacturer’s Ignite conference on Tuesday, CEO Satya Nadella announced Copilot Workspaces, a collaborative, “multiplayer” surface for Copilot’s agentic capabilities.

Also: Microsoft says its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost.

The product, available in Frontier for now, is similar to OpenAI’s ChatGPT Space and several fresh Anthropic features, including Whiteboard and Sheets, which essentially merge the work tools you’re used to using with an agentic framework.

“As the evolution of Copilot Notebooks, it’s where people and agents build on each other’s work,” Microsoft said. “An agent drafts a section of a document, and you review. You leave a comment, and an agent picks it up.”.

Microsoft also announced Autopilot, a sort of counterpoint agent to Copilot that “can watch Teams channels, follow up on emails, run recurring work, and manage a project — without waiting for a prompt,” as Microsoft described.

In a demo video during the keynote, the agent appeared to function similarly to OpenAI’s Dots, but for work — employees can tag their Autopilot “like a colleague,” Microsoft noted, and assign it tasks.

Also: 4 ways Anthropic’s newly introduced Claude Sheets beat using a Google Sheets connector.

Microsoft noted the agent will be able to autonomously handle “meetings and follow-ups on its own,” though that claim may be best verified by teams themselves.

Speaking of trust, however, Microsoft noted that “Autopilot runs on the identity, security, and compliance foundation IT already uses,” and that “each Autopilot has its own Microsoft Entra Agent ID and a named manager,” meaning IT can block it as needed.

According to recent reports, “Its sign-ins and actions are logged under its own name, so security teams have a clear audit trail. Powered by Work IQ, it understands how your organization works within existing permissions,” Microsoft remarked.

The company added that employees will soon “be able to bring their personal Autopilot into Workspaces” as well. The feature is also available in Frontier.

It has been revealed that nadella also announced a few other productivity features, including a “command center” called Today that spans email, calendar, meetings, tasks, and threads in Teams. Right now in private preview in Outlook and the Copilot app, it includes a personalized briefing and a feed of priorities that updates throughout the day.

“The draft is written and ready for you to edit; the schedule change is already proposed; and the forgotten follow-up is waiting for you to send it, complete with context so you can catch up rapidly,” Microsoft mentioned of the feature, which sounds like an agentic briefing-cum-morning-assistant.

Also: Nearly 70% of workers use AI regularly now – but many get no time to upskill.

Microsoft also announced that Home, now generally available, unifies Chat and Cowork into a singular starting point. That’s similar to Anthropic’s recent consolidation of its chat and agentic Cowork offerings, demonstrating an overall trend toward simplification in workplace AI.

While more companies are finally starting to see a return on their AI investment, agents are still expensive and can quickly rack up costs when unsupervised.

Microsoft announced a few tools to track this at Ignite: Agent 365 Business Analytics and Agent 365 Cost Management.

Also: Microsoft wants to put a dollar value on AI’s work – but can you trust the math?

Agent 365, which Microsoft announced last year, is the manufacturer’s observability platform. Microsoft noted Business Analytics, in Frontier Public today, provides insights on what a company is spending on AI and why, and where it’s paying off, as well as forecasts future costs. In a demo during the keynote, Microsoft showed how admins can see when specific agents’ costs have spiked recently and what (human) employee to notify as a result.

In a recent development, “It starts with a latest way to measure your investment: in work completed, not simply tokens,” Microsoft stated. “It analyzes the tasks, how long that work typically takes a person, and the share Cowork performed, providing a sophisticated view of the hours your intelligence supports and what the work is worth.”.

Cost Management lets IT see where teams are using AI down to the model.

Industry observers note that “Leaders can set spending policies, limits, and proactive alerts and control which models are available,” Microsoft mentioned. Anthropic released a similar tool last month, though it was focused more on making seats as efficient as possible on Teams and Enterprise intends.

Tech Report: 1Password Security Incident

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (695 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 1password

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • On November 19, 2026, 1Password began investigating indications that an attacker gained access to an employee’s corporate GitHub account.
  • Industry observers note that the attacker downloaded account records for a subset of our users.
  • Account and user identifiers, and account creation and last sign-in times.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On November 19, 2026, 1Password began investigating indications that an attacker gained access to an employee’s corporate GitHub account. The actor used the account to access source code and push malicious code to backend services, which downloaded administrative data pertaining to our customers. This data included customer names and email addresses, in addition to non-secret internal metadata about the account. At no time were customer vault contents accessed by, or available to, the attacker.

Industry observers note that the attacker downloaded account records for a subset of our users. These records include:.

Account and user identifiers, and account creation and last sign-in times.

Public keys (which are public by design, this has no impact to user security).

Secure Remote Password protocol parameters (which cannot be used to access your account).

Tokens present in certain emailed links for invitations, provisioning and account recovery.

Other non-secret account metadata relative to our internal architecture (e.g. version numeric identifiers, file numeric identifiers).

The attacker also copied source code from private repositories and gained access to our CI/CD system. Our source code is not customer data, and contains no user secrets. CI/CD contains infrastructure related secrets in order for our product to work. We have triggered a rotation of all credentials which may have been exposed, and there is no impact to 1Password’s services, availability, or product security.

Sources indicate that when we send an email to a customer to accept a provisioning invite to an account, or to accept recovery of their account, it contains a token. A provisioning invite is specifically used for our SCIM Bridge or Hosted Provisioning. During this incident there were a small number of customers in this state, who have been specifically notified. This token is used to complete the invitation or recovery process, but only when combined with an SSO sign-in or a six digit code sent to the user's registered email address. The token is not able to get access to the account by itself. In order to reduce the ability for a malicious third party to successfully guess the code, we’ve expanded the code from six numeric digits to ten alphanumeric digits. This makes brute force guessing practically impossible.

Your vaults and the items in them.

The keys that protect your vaults.

1Password does not store your account password or secret key.

1Password apps and browser extensions.

Disabled the affected GitHub account, revoked the stolen token, and removed the access the attacker created.

Rotated or revoked all internal credentials which may have been exposed.

Lengthened the codes used in invitation and recovery emails from six digits to ten characters as a precautionary measure.

Tightened internal GitHub, CI/CD, and endpoint controls, and added new detections for this kind of attack.

Validated no internal evidence of user account takeovers or compromise using any exposed account provisioning tokens.

Brought in independent cybersecurity experts to validate our containment approaches and remediation efforts.

Be cautious about phishing attempts in the form of unexpected emails, texts or calls that mention 1Password, invitations, or account recovery attempts.

Recent findings suggest that 1Password will never contact you to ask for your account password or Secret Key. Only enter them in the official 1Password app, or on our official website, and only when you’ve opened the app or typed the address yourself. Your Secret Key is only needed the first time you sign in on a fresh device or browser.

Keep your Secret Key and account password safe.

If you see something suspicious, tell us at support@1password.com.

You trust us with some of the most sensitive information you have. 1Password is designed so that a breach of our systems can’t expose your vault contents. Your vault secrets are encrypted with keys that only you hold, so we can’t access them, and neither can an attacker who gets into our servers.

In a recent development, we are committed to transparency in the interests of our customers' security and the security of the broader industry, which is why we have published and maintained our Security Whitepaper since 2015. We’ll keep this blog post current, and we’ll enhancement it if we find anything that changes what we’ve noted here.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that during the keynote at its Ignite conference on Tuesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella announced several newly introduced models from Microsoft AI (MAI), its lab within the organization.
  • Also: Microsoft claims its upcoming AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5.
  • MAI mentioned it would allow its customers to customize its frontier models with their own data and run them securely in Azure through an initiative called Licensed Weights.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that during the keynote at its Ignite conference on Tuesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella announced several newly introduced models from Microsoft AI (MAI), its lab within the organization. But new model releases are almost a dime a dozen these days, and accelerating fast — what really stood out was how Microsoft will let its customers access those models.

Also: Microsoft claims its upcoming AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5.

MAI mentioned it would allow its customers to customize its frontier models with their own data and run them securely in Azure through an initiative called Licensed Weights. It’s essentially a selective approach to open-weight AI: more so than proprietary models from OpenAI and Anthropic, but not fully downloadable on Hugging Face like Mistral’s Le Chonk. Interested companies will need to go through their Microsoft account reps to get started.

According to recent reports, “You control who can access it. Your data and adaptations stay entirely yours. And we’ll work with you through Frontier Company to deliver the custom model and embed it in your own products and agents,” Mustafa Suleyman, CEO of MAI, remarked during the keynote.

The approach should stand out to businesses looking for affordable AI that lets them retain control over their IP. Microsoft said it would only use customers’ information to train its models if they agreed.

“No one wants to pour their IQ into someone else’s model,” Suleyman noted during the keynote, a nod to an argument Palantir CEO Alex Karp has made repeatedly.

The dominant, if simplified, narrative in AI has been that proprietary, expensive models boast peak capabilities but aren’t customizable, while open, cheaper models are customizable but less capable. Microsoft’s AI models don’t necessarily compete with OpenAI and Anthropic yet, but the company has legacy sway with countless businesses. By offering a customizable AI option, it could strike a balance among major tech companies.

Western labs, including Thinking Machines and Mistral, are releasing more competitive open-weight models, but Anthropic and OpenAI still have the overwhelming majority of the enterprise AI market. Though Licensed Weights isn’t an open-weight family of models, it does diversify the open-versus-closed debate a bit and differentiate Microsoft’s offering from OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s. It’s also a smart pairing with Microsoft’s goal to balance price and performance, if businesses find it impressive enough.

Also: Microsoft unveiled Copilot Workspaces at Ignite 2026.

“Averaged over four widely used benchmarks that target the everyday enterprise coding tasks we see in GitHub Copilot, MAI Code 2 gives you 98% of the performance of GPT 6.1 Sol at just 40% of the cost, and against Opus 5.5 it’s an incredible 5% of that cost,” Suleyman noted of the new coding model the company confirmed at Ignite.

In a recent development, the tech giant also released its fresh image editing model, MAI Image 2.7, on Tuesday, which now leads the category on Artificial Analysis while beating Nano Banana Pro and several GPT image models on price and quality. With Licensed Weights, Microsoft has positioned itself for organizations seeking a reliable blend of ROI tools, customization, security controls, and capability.

  • A latest report indicates that Apple already has iPads running macOS internally, and that work on a giant iPad continues, but don’t hold your breath for a public launch of either ….
  • Recent findings suggest that as iPad hardware has grown more powerful over the years, the software has struggled to keep up.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With iPads running the same chips as Macs, many have wished Apple would give us the option of running macOS on them instead of the somewhat clunky iPadOS windowing system. Apple’s previous arguments against converging devices have been somewhat weakened by the launch of the touchscreen MacBook Pro.

A latest report indicates that Apple already has iPads running macOS internally, and that work on a giant iPad continues, but don’t hold your breath for a public launch of either ….

Recent findings suggest that as iPad hardware has grown more powerful over the years, the software has struggled to keep up. We saw split-screen capabilities first, with full windowing finally coming to the devices in iPadOS 26 last year.

The UI is still rather clunky compared to macOS, however, leading a significant number of people to wish that Apple simply offered the option of using the more powerful operating system on its tablet devices.

I would be comfortable with 11" and 13" devices running macOS. Actually, I don’t require them to run macOS itself, but I do need them to run macOS apps. I wish the iPad could match a MacBook’s productivity. Running macOS on an iPad seems like a reasonable idea. The MacBook Air is now the better price choice, while those needing a powerhouse will always choose a MacBook Pro or Studio.

Sources indicate that some suggest that running macOS on iPad would reduce Mac sales, but I disagree. I own a nearly full-spec MacBook Pro 16" and expect to keep a machine like that, yet I also purchased a MacBook Air for lighter travel. I would prefer an iPad over the Air, but I cannot choose it because it lacks the apps I require. If it supported them, I would buy the iPad Pro with all accessories, and Apple would gain more revenue from me. I appreciate the concept of owning an iPad, but currently it lacks the value needed to justify paying more for a device that simply does less than a MacBook Air.

In a podcast Q&A, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman states that Apple is already doing this internally, but there’s no sign of any intends to make it available outside the company.

In a recent development, apple has iPads internally running macOS, and they’ve had that for some time. The fact that they have the underlying architecture of Apple Silicon that’s the same on the iPad and the Mac gives them the flexibility in order to test these types of things.

In terms if they’re actually going to do it – would they bring macOS to the iPad itself – at this point I don’t think that’s going to happen anytime soon. I’ve checked into this and there’s no ongoing operating system project right now in terms of a brand new operating system for the iPad – there is no work being done to consumerize macOs on the iPad.

Gurman says Apple seems set to continue to make piecemeal changes over time to bring iPad capabilities closer to those of the Mac but is showing no signs of full convergence.

He reiterated that work on a long-rumored giant-sized folding iPad continues.

It has been revealed that the other thing I want to say is that I’m really excited for this potential of Project J312. That is, this giant 19-inch, 20-inch foldable iPad. And it’s basically like a gigantic iPhone Duo with no display on the outside.

Industry observers note that however, he says there’s no guarantee it will ever launch, saying the timings have already slipped from 2027 through 2028 to 2029, but both cost and yield problems may still kill the project. If it does launch, it’s expected to cost anywhere from $3,000 to $5,000.

According to recent reports, ubuntu 27.04, Tenacious T-Rex, is set for an April 22, 2027 release. Although that seems a long way off, it’s sooner than you think. As is implied by the release number, 27.04 is not an LTS release, so it only receives support for nine months (until January 2028). The good news is that you can migrate from 27.04 to 27.10, and then to the LTS release, 28.04. The entire upgrade path ensures that you don’t have to miss a single release.

But what’s coming in Ubuntu 27.04? Given that it’s an interim release, you’re probably assuming that there’ll be nothing exciting to be found. Although there won’t be any game-changing additions, there will be plenty of refinements and bug fixes.

Also: I’ve used Ubuntu for 22 years – and 26.10 might be its best release yet.

It has been revealed that I’ve been using the daily release of Ubuntu 27.04 for a bit. Let’s take a look at what is currently expected in Tenacious T-Rex.

In a recent development, this is probably the biggest addition to the next release of Ubuntu. And although you won’t find any major changes in GNOME, there are some important ones. First off, there will be editable quick settings, which allow for customizing, adding, removing, and rearranging toggles and widgets. GNOME 52 will also enjoy a revamped calendar popover, which streamlines the feature to focus primarily on events, time, and weather.

Also: Over Ubuntu? Fedora is the Linux distro I’d hop to next – here’s why.

There will also be several improvements to window management, such as a spatial overview and a mosaic/tiling system for auto-resizing and organizing windows, a refined full-screen Alt+Tab app switcher, which will be capable of grouping older windows by application while showing newer ones individually, and finally, the ability to remember window sizing, placement, and workspace.

Recent findings suggest that desktop search is also getting a bit of polish by way of a redesigned popover and an improved results overlay that includes file previews, multiple actions, and search filters. And, as usual, there will be plenty of bug fixes and performance enhancements. The bump in speed is noticeable, too, in my testing.

Ubuntu 27.04 will ship with the Linux 7.6 kernel, which includes better VRAM management for gaming and expanded support for modern hardware, such as early enablement for AMD Zen 6, stable support for Intel Xe3P, mainline boot capabilities for Apple M3 Pro/Max/Ultra, and initial support for the 2026 Steam Controller.

There will also be performance gains for both the Btrfs and Ext4 file systems, which (along with the improvements in GNOME 52) will make Ubuntu 27.04 one of the best-performing releases in some time.

I will say this: I’ve come to count on Ubuntu’s latest releases to be an improvement over the previous iterations, and from what I’ve seen so far in my testing, 27.04 will not disappoint. 📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, black Friday shopping can be exhausting, especially when you're juggling multiple wish lists, comparing prices and trying to stick to a budget.
  • On Tuesday, Walmart revealed a partnership with Meta that lets customers shop its Black Friday deals through Muse, Meta's personal AI agent.
  • It has been revealed that unlike traditional AI chatbots that recommend products and send you links, Muse can take you through the purchasing process without leaving the conversation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, black Friday shopping can be exhausting, especially when you're juggling multiple wish lists, comparing prices and trying to stick to a budget. But this year, Walmart is giving shoppers the option to hand some of that work over to AI.

On Tuesday, Walmart revealed a partnership with Meta that lets customers shop its Black Friday deals through Muse, Meta's personal AI agent.

It has been revealed that unlike traditional AI chatbots that recommend products and send you links, Muse can take you through the purchasing process without leaving the conversation. Of course, you'll still have to actually approve the purchase, but it could be helpful when time is of the essence.

And if you're nervous about giving AI access to your credit card, Walmart has built in some safeguards.

Let's say you're looking for a blender but you don't want to spend your entire afternoon comparing models. You can tell Muse what you're looking for, how much you're willing to spend and whether you need it delivered.

Walmart handles the product matching behind the scenes through its new Agent Gateway.

According to the retailer, shoppers will have access to the same prices available on Walmart.com, including Black Friday discounts and applicable membership benefits.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Walmart also indicates the integration doesn't expose your broader shopping history to third-party agents.

In a recent development, I decided to give this a try (hopefully my husband isn't reading this). I started by simply heading to Muse.ai. From there, I described what I wanted. You can be as descriptive as you want or even vague. I simply gave the prompt, "My husband does a lot of yard work and I'd like to find a gift to help make the job easier." I didn't give a budget (it prompted me "what's your budget?) or any other specific requirements, but you can up front to make shopping even more personal and streamlined. Once you've done that, you're going to want to do the following:.

Connect your Walmart account. Muse will direct you to Walmart to sign in before returning you to the conversation.

Sources indicate that set your spending limit. When adding your first product, you'll create a Walmart Agent Profile to manage what the AI is authorized to do.

Complete your purchase. You can check out directly through the conversation with your existing Walmart payment method.Muse demonstrated me a few items before completing the purchase. Rest assured it does pause so you can see the choices. My husband has many of the items on the list already, so that hesitation was appreciated. Since my credit card is already connected to Walmart, this safeguard is vital. The last thing I want is to spend hundreds of dollars on yard equipment we already have!

Walmart's regular return policy still applies to purchases made through Muse.

The more specific you are about what you need, the more useful AI shopping could be. If you're looking for someone on your list who is difficult to shop for like a teenage boy, this Muse partnership could be a lifesaver. Here are five prompts worth trying.

"Find me the best Black Friday deal on a 55-inch 4K TV under $300 at Walmart.".

"Help me buy Christmas gifts for three kids ages 6, 9 and 12 with a total budget of $150.".

"Find five tech gifts under $25 that are currently discounted at Walmart.".

"Find the best Black Friday deals on wireless headphones under $100. Prioritize battery life and noise cancellation.".

"Help me find stocking stuffers for four people without spending more than $50 total.".

I'd recommend including instructions to show you the individual prices and total cost before completing any purchase.

Between shopping lists, crowded stores and seemingly endless Black Friday sales, there's certainly an appeal to having AI take care of some of the legwork.

But I'd still recommend double-checking product specifications, customer reviews and prices at competing retailers before letting an AI agent make a purchase. Just because something is discounted doesn't necessarily mean it's the best deal.

It has been revealed that walmart notes it plans to bring its shopping experience to additional AI agents and apps in the future. For now, Muse offers another way to tackle your holiday shopping list without opening dozens of browser tabs.

It has been revealed that some of the most popular Android smartwatches just got a battery-saving revision. Google released an updated version of Google Play Services on Tuesday that can help extend the battery life of a Wear OS smartwatch.

Recent findings suggest that the v26.45 enhancement concerns location tracking during outdoor workouts. Wear OS smartwatch users can now use their phone’s Global Navigation Satellite System to track their location during an outdoor workout, which can conserve battery life by outsourcing the smartwatch’s energy to the smartphone when it isn’t in Battery Saver mode.

Sources indicate that also: Pixel Watch 4 vs. Watch 5: Is Google’s upcoming model worth it?

Constantly communicating with satellites during an outdoor workout can be a battery drain, and every minute of battery life counts when you use your smartwatch for communication, workout tracking, and health monitoring. GPS services, a bright, always-on display, and continuous health sensors like SpO2 can squeeze the most juice out of your smartwatch.

Wear OS software is used by many of the most popular smartwatch brands, including Google, Samsung, and OnePlus. Both the Google Pixel Watch and Samsung Galaxy Watch’s largest batteries last approximately 40 hours. That’s nearly two days of use from two top Android smartwatches, but you’d be surprised how rapidly it can drain.

Also: Galaxy Watch 9 review: Health data overload, but built for the future.

The update improves battery life without users having to take any action or change any settings — the Google Play Services version 26.45 works quietly under the hood.

In a recent development, that’s not the only Google Play Services update that Wear OS smartwatch users can take advantage of. Another recent update lets users view on their phone a larger preview of any watch face they want to install on their smartwatch.

Here are some of the key findings from the 2026 holiday shopping research.

It has been revealed that retailers that use AI shopping agents are seeing bigger orders and more loyal customers. The survey found that shoppers who use AI agent referrals are twice as likely to make a purchase. In addition, 39% of shoppers have used AI agents on an e-commerce site, and 80% had a positive experience, while 75% felt more loyal to the brand as a result of the AI agent experience.

Shoppers who use AI agents spend 8% more than the average buyer and purchase 23% more items per order. Brands that use AI agents are seeing seven times faster sales growth than brands without them.

It has been revealed that the survey found that 28% of consumers give their agents multiple tasks per day. The most common use of AI agents is price comparisons, product reviews, and brainstorming for gift items. Brand discovery is a major benefit of AI agent use cases.

In a recent development, agents as advisors are growing, but agents are not buying products yet, with only 19% of personal agent consumers using logic to check out. Only 9% of consumers allow their personal AI agents to have unrestricted access to their financial details, and 36% have set up a separate credit card for their AI agents.

The majority of consumers (73%) are not comfortable giving personal AI agents their payment information, and 49% are not interested in agents making purchases on their behalf. Consumers do not want to share their purchase history or personal data that could potentially lead to unwanted charges. Shoppers will abandon an AI agent after 2-3 mistakes. If an AI agent makes a bad recommendation, 1 in 3 consumers will blame the AI.

Retailers must adopt AI shopping agents in order to compete. Retailers must be able to service and respond to shopper agents. The ability to detect intent, buying signals, sources of dissatisfaction, and other consumer-related buying patterns at machine scale (significantly faster and higher volume than human scale) will require retailers to invest in AI agentic engagement capabilities.

  • Recent findings suggest that just months after its release, Google is making its Spark agent free and officially renaming its capabilities “Tasks.” You can now toggle to it from the standard Gemini Chat setting.
  • According to recent reports, also: Ready for a Siri AI agent?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that just months after its release, Google is making its Spark agent free and officially renaming its capabilities “Tasks.” You can now toggle to it from the standard Gemini Chat setting. Reports show the rebrand started gradually in mid-October.

According to recent reports, also: Ready for a Siri AI agent? Apple under pressure to upgrade its assistant faster.

OpenAI offers its Dots agents as part of its $100 per month ChatGPT Pro tier, and Anthropic’s Claude Duet is available with paid plans, which start at $20 per month. That makes Tasks and Meta Muse — the latter was called the “worst AI agent for privacy” by ZDNET’s David Gewirtz — Big Tech’s most affordable personal agents on the market, though you’ll have to pay for more than five hours of access at a time.

If Tasks sounds familiar, it should: The tech giant already has a product called Google Tasks, which lets you turn emails into a checkable to-do list on the side of your inbox, among other places like Chat and Docs. This is the agentic version, obviously.

Gewirtz, ZDNET’s AI tester-in-residence, wasn’t blown away by then-Spark when he tried it last month, but had reason to believe in its eventual improvement. It’s unclear whether Tasks is meaningfully different from Spark, aside from being out of beta.

Abilities aside, what sets Tasks apart here is cost. Dots and Duet haven’t exactly impressed thus far, so free alternatives don’t have a high bar to reach yet.

Also: I tested OpenAI Dot and Anthropic Duet for weeks.

During Gewirtz’s test, when the agent was part of his $20 per month Google AI Pro blueprint, he used only 20% of the total five hours of usage on “four fairly substantial tests.” Without an AI plan, Gemini’s context window is 32k tokens.

At launch in September, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg mentioned Muse is “free to use for up to 100M tokens per week,” though Meta’s help center is not so explicit. As with most agentic products, more frequent customers may want to buy more access, but more casual users now have two options to compare.

According to recent reports, AI companies are vying to hook customers with their various personal agents, and price and privacy are major factors to consider. Being free with limits, Muse and Tasks are perhaps geared toward a more apprehensive user who wants to try an agent, but isn’t giving it countless tasks to take on all day. Given Muse’s reputation, some may find Tasks a bit less aggressive or risky.

Also: Don’t use Muse? How Meta’s AI agent can still access your private messages.

According to recent reports, as with other agents, Tasks, which runs on its newest Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, can handle a variety of jobs for you, from grocery shopping to booking appointments and analyzing your heating bill. Agents like these are designed for a chronically overwhelmed society trained by a reliance on tech to seek convenience and productivity in nearly every aspect of life.

It has been revealed that the feature is free in the US, Canada, Korea, Japan, Australia, and India. US users can also start tasks by emailing or texting Gemini, and can have the agent call businesses for them (except in Indiana, Louisiana, Minnesota, Montana, and Nebraska).

Industry observers note that the change from Spark to Tasks comes just a day after Google retired Gems (which let you tailor Gemini to specific tasks), and converted existing Gems into Skills. The newly introduced landing page for Tasks emphasizes personal finance and cost-cutting as a use case, positioning itself alongside personal finance features from Anthropic and OpenAI.

“Put Gemini on the hunt for ways to save. Identify recurring expenses you no longer need, get alerts for your most-desired deals, and more,” the page reads.

AI agents remain a privacy and security risk, because of their ability to autonomously and proactively handle tasks like placing orders (which you can set spending caps for) and reviewing files.

Also: Want to try ChatGPT Wallet? Read OpenAI’s liability disclaimer.

“You can adjust task settings, disconnect Google and third-party apps, or delete chat history anytime,’ Google’s blog on the release stated. Google’s newly introduced Memory summary feature for Gemini lets customers view and edit the personal info the chatbot has on them.

#108302. Can an App Tell When Someone Near You Is Wearing Smart Glasses?

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1291 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

Can an App Tell When Someone Near You Is Wearing Smart Glasses?

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1291 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Meta’s smart glasses stay connected to the wearer’s phone over Bluetooth, and that connection is what detector apps look for.
  • In a recent development, it’s a clever workaround for glasses designed to blend in.
  • Here’s how those apps work, what they reliably catch and what they miss.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Meta’s smart glasses stay connected to the wearer’s phone over Bluetooth, and that connection is what detector apps look for. Apps such as Zuckoff scan for the short broadcast signals Bluetooth devices send out and compare them with signals from known smart glasses models. When there’s a match, the app sends an alert. It’s a practical way to learn that a pair is nearby, though the alert can’t confirm whether anyone’s recording, and glasses with Bluetooth switched off won’t appear at all. Here’s how the apps work and how much weight to give an alert.

In a recent development, it’s a clever workaround for glasses designed to blend in. How useful it is depends on what you want it to tell you: The app can detect that a pair is close by, but not whether it’s recording. Still, that’s more notice than most people get today, especially if they haven’t spotted the glasses’ built-in LED indicator.

Here’s how those apps work, what they reliably catch and what they miss.

Broad concerns over privacy have led to a technical battle. On one side, hardware modifiers are tweaking wearable cameras to make them even harder to spot, often by disabling LED indicators. On the other, developers and privacy-focused coders are launching counter tech to give you a heads-up when a hidden camera walks into the room.

Zuckoff, whose name takes a direct jab at Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, has joined a small ecosystem of apps such as Antizuck Smart Glasses Scanner and Nearby Glasses that offer similar functionality — letting you know when someone has smart glasses activated and how close the device is, although they can’t tell you specifically whether someone is actively recording or using AI to pull up information. The apps detect approximate device proximity by sweeping local Bluetooth frequencies to locate vendor IDs, system identifiers and hardware signatures associated with smart glasses.

It has been revealed that as Zuckoff’s website notes: “Glasses advertise loudest while powering on, pairing or leaving the case. Once paired to their owner’s phone, they can go quiet, so silence is not proof that nobody is recording, and a detection is not proof that anyone is. Signal strength gives a rough distance and no direction at all.”.

Zuckoff’s developer, Pawel Szydlowski, mentioned he was already working on projects that used Bluetooth to detect nearby devices and discovered the tech could be applied to smart glasses. “It’s just the same technology wrapped in a different paper,” he said in a video chat with CNET.

Recent reports have shown that smart glasses are being used for everything from bullying in schools to viral videos with unwitting subjects who don’t know they’re being recorded.

What drove Szydlowski to actively develop a software detector was seeing social media videos of people wearing smart glasses who recorded pranks or harassed women with pickup lines. None of the targets seemed aware that their content would appear online, which made Szydlowski angry. “There was not even a blur involved to try to censor them, to give them some sort of feeling of privacy,” he mentioned. “These days, everybody feels entitled to post everything.”.

It has been revealed that since it launched in early August, the Zuckoff app has gotten 2,000 sign-ups, and Szydlowski is beta-testing an Android version he hopes to make available on the Google Play Store. The app also has a premium version for $10 a year that can run continuous detection checks in the background when the app isn’t in use.

But a booming ecosystem of DIY modifications and third-party hardware hacks is also giving smart glasses wearers unprecedented stealth by allowing them to disable the activation lights, either by bypassing the capture LEDs or by patching software to suppress system notifications.

Tech journalist Joanna Stern hosted a video showing the process in which a local hacker removed the LED light from her Ray-Ban Meta glasses for $100, allowing the wearables to secretly record without notice.

According to recent reports, detecting active smart glasses in public or private spaces adds a new layer of security awareness, but it raises an obvious dilemma: What do you actually do with that information? Once a detector app alerts us that smart glasses are nearby, it seems our only choices are to either leave the space or ask the wearer to remove the glasses.

Sources indicate that uttara Ananthakrishnan, an associate professor of information systems at the University of Washington who studies the societal impacts of technology, says we’re still figuring out the social norms around wearables like smart glasses. It’s impossible to know whether the person filming will behave responsibly, and the question of consent gets even thornier if children might be captured on video or in photos.

Unlike with smartphones, where it’s easier to tell when someone is recording or taking photos, “smart glasses shift the burden of privacy entirely onto the person being photographed,” Ananthakrishnan said.

“Until we develop clear mechanisms to balance seamless innovation with consent, these devices will continue to turn everyday public spaces into zones of surveillance anxiety,” she noted.

That surveillance anxiety may prompt some hardware makers to release alternative versions of smart glasses that entirely avoid potential privacy violations.

The Even G2 smart glasses don’t have a camera for recording photos or videos. They can pair with a separately sold R1 control ring that works as a fitness tracker.

Sources indicate that for instance, Even Realities’ G2 smart glasses don’t include a front-facing camera at all. Instead, the Even G2 devices, released in late 2025, focus on providing the wearer with information and acting more like a personal assistant.

It has been revealed that “We made the decision from the beginning that smart glasses don’t need to have cameras on them in order to be useful,” Even Realities CEO Will Wang told CNET in an email. “We believe something worn on your face should respect not only the person wearing it, but everyone around them.”.

Recent findings suggest that the G2 devices don’t record externally, a design choice Wang said gave the company a unique challenge. “Leaving the camera out also pushed us to think differently about what actually makes smart glasses useful day to day, rather than assuming more sensors automatically make a better product,” he said.

Industry observers note that wang said there’s room in the smart glasses market for different approaches to features and functionality, and that buyers may want to make trade-offs for devices they’ll wear on their faces. But Wang noted that the rise of smart glasses detectors indicates that social acceptance is an glitch the industry needs to consider.

According to recent reports, over the last several months, smart glasses have been getting cheaper. And with more models and companies jumping into the fray, the demand for surveillance detectors is likely to grow — that is, unless Significant Tech and wearable companies radically change their devices to make them invisible to detector apps.

Zuckoff’s Szydlowski mentioned it’s possible a organization could shrink the kind of 5G technology to fit in smart glasses, making them less dependent on phones and Bluetooth, but that’s unlikely to happen anytime soon. If Meta or Snap deliberately updated their hardware to hide from detection apps and disable smart glasses’ digital footprint, it would further undercut any claim of privacy accountability.

It has been revealed that szydlowski stated his hope is that, in time, Zuckoff won’t be needed at all. He pointed out that the ability to detect nearby Apple AirTag devices eventually became part of the operating systems on iOS and Android devices. If consumers pressure manufacturers and their governments to make smart glasses easier to detect, it would be “the perfect solution” to make his app obsolete, he said.

Nothing’s AI Earbuds Will Serve as an All-in-One Conversation Recorder

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (709 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, phone-maker Nothing Technology is breaking away from its typical retro-inspired designs with a new pair of AI-powered earbuds, as reported earlier by Bloomberg.
  • The Ear Note earbuds are designed primarily to maximize the recording functionality.
  • Sources indicate that the earbuds can capture and transcribe phone calls, while the charging case has its own microphone to record in-person conversations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, phone-maker Nothing Technology is breaking away from its typical retro-inspired designs with a new pair of AI-powered earbuds, as reported earlier by Bloomberg. The firm confirmed via an X post that its Ear Note wireless earbuds will be available starting Dec. 8.

The Ear Note earbuds are designed primarily to maximize the recording functionality. While other AI earbuds have already hit the market, the Ear Note is the first to record both phone calls and in-person conversations.

Sources indicate that the earbuds can capture and transcribe phone calls, while the charging case has its own microphone to record in-person conversations. To mitigate privacy concerns, the case only records with a physical button press — a tell that could reveal when audio is being captured around the Ear Note user.

Nothing shared that the Ear Note will work with multiple popular AI agents, but the full list of compatible software has not yet been released. The Ear Note works in tandem with an app that stores recordings from the earbuds and case, creating transcriptions and summaries similar to those created by the popular Otter AI app.

The Nothing brand has developed a cult following for combining lifestyle and fashion trends in its suite of smartphones, headphones, speakers and watches.

Recent findings suggest that the full product lineup is built with modern hardware, but mimics warm, nearly retrofuturist design sensibilities. The blocky Ear Note charging case continues this trend while taking the manufacturer’s tech in a new direction.

In the lead-up to the Ear Note’s reveal, Nothing CEO Carl Pei described the earbuds in an X post as “a tool, but one built with the personality and care that have come to define a Nothing product.”.

In a Bloomberg interview, Pei indicated that Nothing isn’t trying to create AI agents or software, but that the manufacturer has a “really interesting opportunity to be the hardware layer to AI.”.

It’s currently unclear how much the Ear Note earbuds and case will cost when they’re released next month. According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, the company hasn’t settled on a price just yet. The most expensive earbuds currently available on the Nothing store cost $149.

In a recent development, whether you’re covering your eyes, plugging your ears or slapping a timepiece on your wrist, there’s now an ever-present option to record the world around you. Multiple companies have created their own versions of smart glasses, earbuds and watches with augmented reality capabilities.

It has been revealed that now that AI is the flavor du jour, these existing features are being enhanced by new ways to scan and interact with the surrounding environment. That means a lot of visual and auditory data is being recorded by wearable devices, and very rarely with the consent of all parties involved.

The most immediate risk factors are associated with video recording – public distrust of smart glasses is so widespread that they’ve colloquially been coined “pervert glasses,” as folks fear they fundamentally break an unspoken social contract by obscuring public recording from other people.

But audio recording, enabled by Apple’s latest smartwatches, the Amazon Bee, Plaud earbuds and the latest Ear Note, is also raising concerns, not least because many states require all-party consent before you can record conversations.

In a recent development, the Ear Note’s ability to record every bit of audio, from phone calls to in-person conversations, means it will be handling more sensitive information than other AI-powered earbuds. The company will need to face new challenges to ensure security measures are in place to prevent private chats from leaking.

Sources indicate that at the very least, it seems as though Nothing Technology is aware of these privacy risks. According to Bloomberg, the manufacturer created a data and security team to address concerns that cropped up during the Ear Note’s development. The company has also “obtained the same privacy certifications as competing recording products and worked with law firms to assess potential risks and safeguards.”.

Pei called wearables with recording functionality a sensitive space, and said the design team was “extra careful to not take any risks.” The Ear Note earbuds and case are largely controlled by user commands, including tactile button presses that begin the recording process.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that the Google Wallet app is available for iPhone people in the US for the first time.
  • Also: You can use Google’s Spark AI agent, renamed Tasks, for free now – with limits.
  • Recent findings suggest that the new Google Wallet app lets you digitize physical cards, including payment, loyalty, and membership cards, as well as boarding passes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the Google Wallet app is available for iPhone people in the US for the first time. iOS users who download the newly introduced Google Wallet app can manage online payments for faster checkout at places that support Google Pay. However, Apple restricts Google’s ability to offer tap-to-pay service on the iOS app, so users won’t be able to use Google Wallet for contactless checkout on iPhone.

Also: You can use Google’s Spark AI agent, renamed Tasks, for free now – with limits.

Recent findings suggest that the new Google Wallet app lets you digitize physical cards, including payment, loyalty, and membership cards, as well as boarding passes. Google Wallet app users on iOS will also be able to view receipts and track orders pulled from Gmail in one app.

There used to be a Google Pay app for iOS, but it was discontinued in 2024. The old Google Pay app also didn’t support tap-to-pay on iPhone, but it offered limited functionality, including support for loyalty and gift cards, as well as purchase tracking.

The biggest difference between the old Google Pay app for iOS and the upcoming Google Wallet is the AI component, which supports agentic shopping, likely as Google’s longer-term play.

One of Google’s goals for the Wallet app on iOS is to make it a central place to manage purchases made by its AI agents. The Agents section in Google Wallet for iPhone lets you manage and monitor purchases made through Gemini.

It has been revealed that agentic commerce is on the rise, as evidenced by the growing use of Meta’s Muse. Gemini can make purchases and payments through the Tasks feature, which lets you give Gemini permission to buy the items you want and set your maximum budget.

Also: Google Wallet just turned your Android phone into a digital house key.

Recent findings suggest that the Google Wallet app for iOS becomes the central hub for purchase management in agentic commerce through Gemini. In it, you can view active tasks to see which purchases Gemini is working on, as well as completed purchases and receipts.

Google has been working on two technologies to support its agentic commerce strategy: Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) and Agent Payments Protocol (AP2).

UCP is a technical language that enables AI agents to communicate with retailers and make purchases, while AP2 is the payment framework that establishes rules and authorization for agents to make payments.

Google Wallet serves as both the AI-powered wallet and the consumer-facing record of transactions made by Gemini.

Also: Google Wallet has a lot of upcoming tricks – these 5 are my favorites.

Along with Google, major retailers supported the development of UCP, including Shopify, Walmart, Target, and Etsy. When Google announced AP2, more than 60 organizations became involved, including PayPal, Salesforce, Mastercard, and American Express.

Apple has a new MacBook Air with M6 chip coming early next year, but per Mark Gurman on his latest podcast episode, a “major MacBook Air overhaul” could launch as early as 2027 too. Here’s what he noted.

Today on the latest episode of Mark Gurman’s Power On podcast, the well-sourced reporter answered a listener question that involves the future of the MacBook Air.

When asked about the next-generation MacBook Air, here’s what Gurman stated:.

The next MacBook Air project, J913 and J915, the 13-inch version and the 15-inch version, that is coming in spring 2027 alongside the MacBook Neo 2. And this is going to be another “chip and ship,” so a chip refresh.

And we are getting to the end of the road here for the current MacBook Air design. The current MacBook Air design was introduced in ’22, was refreshed in ’23 with the 15-inch model. We’re now in 2027. MacBook Air is Apple’s most popular computer, and they need to keep it very fresh. And so my anticipation is 2027-2028 is when we’re going to get the big MacBook Air overhaul. And I think OLED will be part of that conversation.

There are several noteworthy takeaways here:.

In a recent development, it would be unusual for Apple to launch two distinct MacBook Air models in the same calendar year. However, if that does happen, it would follow the exact same playbook Apple used with the MacBook Pro this year.

Recent findings suggest that this March, a latest MacBook Pro rolled out with M5 Pro and M5 Max chips but the same design that’s been around since 2021. Then in October, Apple unveiled the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display and a new industrial design.

It sounds like a very similar rollout could happen for the MacBook Air in 2027.
