Breaking: Claude can ship code for you now – how to try it (if you dare)

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (899 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, developers are already using Claude Code and other AI-powered coding tools like OpenAI’s Codex in droves, but some still want to check code themselves before pushing it.
  • Recent findings suggest that with Claude Ship, declared in beta Monday, “Claude can now review pull requests, fix them, and approve the ones that a team’s policy allows,” Anthropic noted.
  • Also: How I made a paid Mac app in 11 days with Claude – without writing a single line of code.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, developers are already using Claude Code and other AI-powered coding tools like OpenAI’s Codex in droves, but some still want to check code themselves before pushing it. A new feature from Anthropic is banking on more adventurous, agent-first coders being comfortable with handing even that last step off to AI.

Recent findings suggest that with Claude Ship, declared in beta Monday, “Claude can now review pull requests, fix them, and approve the ones that a team’s policy allows,” Anthropic noted. The feature is geared toward individual developers or companies who want to move faster or already delegate a significant amount of coding tasks to agents.

Also: How I made a paid Mac app in 11 days with Claude – without writing a single line of code.

“Teams stay in control of where it runs and which changes need a person,” Anthropic said. “The goal: ship code as fast as teams write it.”.

It has been revealed that the latest feature uses two new agents alongside Code Review, which Anthropic released in March for Teams and Enterprise intends. Code Review first collects, organizes, and posts findings to a PR. Then, Anthropic mentioned, the agents, PR Steward and Claude Approvals, guide a PR “through review, fixes, and an approval decision so teams don’t have to manage each step manually.”.

PR Steward can’t approve or merge pull requests, designed instead to participate “on failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and review feedback from Code Review, other review tools, or team members.” It also documents what it changed in each push through comments and provides instructions for how to undo it, should developers want to. Throughout the process, developers can give Claude instructions or tell it to stop by commenting @claude.

Also: I tried replacing Claude Code with a local AI stack that’s completely free – how it went.

As a final step, Claude Approvals references whatever policy the user or team abides by (which developers provide as a repo file), and additional signals developers set, like Code Review findings, before approving changes autonomously if allowed. If not, it will seek out “deeper human sign-off,” Anthropic remarked.

Industry observers note that “It works like a smarter CODEOWNERS file,” the release added. Anthropic noted it recommends that most customers enable those additional checks “first in observe-only mode to build confidence before configuring branch protection to require Claude Approvals’ green light.”.

Admins can select which repos the feature runs in and adjust settings as needed.

But Claude Ship isn’t meant for everyone.

Industry observers note that “Most teams want a person to approve every change, and that’s easy to keep up with when people write every line. But a lot of developers build with agents now,” Anthropic said in the release, noting that its own Claude Code team uses Claude to write a majority of the code it needs.

ZDNET senior contributing editor David Gewirtz said the idea of shipping code at the speed of writing it “raises the hair on the back of my neck.” But he added that, given how impressive Claude Code has been thus far, he wouldn’t be surprised if Anthropic’s deployment tools were equally effective.

According to recent reports, also: Claude Code vs. Codex: Why I use both and how to choose one (if you must).

“But, it does depend on the team’s workflow and the kind of development they’re doing,” he stated. “It’s not something for every team and certainly not for every indy developer, but for certain deployment processes, it could shave a ton of time off turnaround, saving money and potentially sending fixes to customers much faster. ‘Tis cool.”.

Ultimately, Gewirtz noted he has reasons to both trust the tool and be concerned about what it means for younger developers in the workplace.

“Since that workflow is often assigned to less experienced members of the team, it’s likely that Claude would be as accurate, although it’s one more way to shut the junior members out of where they add value to the tech giant and grow their skills to become senior decision makers,” he said.

According to recent reports, developer platforms overall are adapting to the fresh state of the industry. Entire, a GitHub competitor started by the Microsoft-owned platform’s former CEO, is built around the expectation that developers are working side-by-side with agents.

Individuals with a Pro, Max, or Ultra subscription can use the /ship command now available in Claude Code, meaning “customers won’t notice any significant increase in token usage,” an Anthropic representative explained. Team and Enterprise users can use Claude Ship for Github repos, and it is billed on tokens, so your overall bill may change.

Still, that depends on the number of PRs users are putting through Claude Ship — to avoid any surprises, admins can set spending limits for both Code Review and the upcoming PR Steward agent. They can also turn Claude Ship on for an entire repo, meaning developers won’t need the /ship command.

Anthropic added that certain Enterprise organizations “can claim at least $10,000 in Claude Ship credits to use within 30 days of claiming” by Jan. 15, 2027.

Also: How I safely run my OpenClaw AI agent 24/7 on a Mac – with Claude Code standing guard.

As with other Claude features, like the still-to-come Meetings, customers with a zero-data-retention policy and other privacy configurations don’t have access to Claude Ship.

Latest Update: This Is What My Apple Watch Heard When I Let It Evesdrop on My Conversations

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1219 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, no, your phone isn’t listening to you.
  • Along with the general sensor, processor, and battery upgrades, the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 introduced Audio Intelligence, a upcoming set of features that allows the watch to listen in on conversations.
  • Siri Recap generates summaries of what you’ve discussed throughout the day, while Live Rewind gives you a transcript of the last 15 seconds of audio in case you missed something.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, no, your phone isn’t listening to you. But what about your Apple Watch? I’ve been testing fresh Audio Intelligence features that record conversations around me, and despite how disturbing it may sound to have your smartwatch listening and taking notes of your entire day, the reality has been a lot more mundane.

Along with the general sensor, processor, and battery upgrades, the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 introduced Audio Intelligence, a upcoming set of features that allows the watch to listen in on conversations.

Siri Recap generates summaries of what you’ve discussed throughout the day, while Live Rewind gives you a transcript of the last 15 seconds of audio in case you missed something.

It’s similar functionality as AI-powered recording pins like Plaud or Amazon’s Bee, but within the context of your smartwatch and without the additional cost or subscription.

And it’s completely optional. You have to first opt-in to the features to activate them, then choose to turn the feature you want on whenever you want to start using it. Then you can leave it on all day, set it on a schedule or toggle it manually whenever you need it. If you’re like me and forget that it’s on, you get reminders that it’s still listening or to check your recaps.

The fact that you have so much control over whether you use it and how much helped ease the creepy factor for me, but there’s still everyone else to consider.

Beyond a barely audible chime when I double-click the Digital Crown to activate Live Rewind, there’s no way to alert others that the feature is in use and that whoever’s in earshot is inadvertently getting roped into my little experiment as well. Other wearables like smart glasses have an indicator light on the front to alert spectators when they’re recording video.

Industry observers note that apple has built-in privacy safeguards for the audio, how it’s processed and then deleted. I’ve broken all that down in a separate Audio Intelligence FAQ. This is about what it’s like to use it in the wild.

I’ve been testing Audio Intelligence in the WatchOS 27.3 (and iOS) public beta for two weeks. Because this isn’t the final version (Apple indicates it will release publicly later this year), consider this a sneak preview.

Let’s get Live Rewind out of the way because there’s not a lot to say about it. Whether from a lack of muscle memory (or usefulness), I’ve had to go out of my way to remember the feature exists.

Sources indicate that I figured it’d come in handy for those “come again?” moments during conversations, but the reality is that it’s just easier to ask someone to repeat what they noted than remember to double-press the Digital Crown at just the right moment. I can see it being more useful when you’re listening to a presentation or other event.

Recent findings suggest that fifteen seconds go by a lot faster than I expect and by the time I realize something might be worth revisiting, the person has moved on with the conversation. I either missed what I intended to get or just captured the silence after.

Siri Recap has been more useful, though it’s still hit-or-miss. The feature gives you high-level summaries of what it heard — it doesn’t provide a transcript to review, and it doesn’t identify who mentioned what. It shines brightest during dedicated meetings when there’s a single conversation to follow rather than a jumble of unrelated discussions.

One success story: I was moderating the chat for our iPhone Duo live folding test on YouTube while Matthew Murray, CNET’s lab director, answered viewer questions on the stream.

I thought I’d caught the gist of what he was saying, but the typing must’ve distracted me more than I realized because I was pleasantly surprised to learn some interesting facts that I’d missed in the Siri Recap, like “Opening a phone 20 times daily over 10 years equals 73,000 folds” or that the “machine runs approximately 22,560 cycles every 24 hours”.

But Siri’s batting average wasn’t always that good, which made it challenging to trust the notes. During a conversation with another mom about car-pool logistics, Siri Recap pulled out action items, like who I was picking up and at what time, which I appreciated, but the information wasn’t accurate. Not only had Siri gotten the names of the kids wrong, it also had me picking up the wrong kid. Clearly, the mental load of figuring out after-school logistics is challenging even for Siri.

Siri can’t handle the messy conversations (and TV indicates).

Where things get interesting (and occasionally hilarious) is how Siri discerns what constitutes a conversation and how many topics belong in a single recap.

Siri is generally good at accurately labeling what conversations are about: “Parent-teacher conferences,” “Car-pool logistics,” “Folding phone durability testing.” But rather than keeping them separate, as it should, it sometimes conflates two or even three completely unrelated conversations into a single recap.

Sources indicate that I encountered bullet points summarizing a serious conversation with a friend about a medical condition alongside notes about a chaotic (albeit funny) exploding apple cider incident with my kids. The two conversations happened within the same two-hour window, but they were by no means back-to-back.

It’s a good thing Siri Recap leaves out tone and volume cause that last bullet would’ve been in ALL CAPS.

Industry observers note that what it did decide was worthy of a standalone recap was a discussion about wedding looks during an episode of Nobody Wants This on Netflix. To be fair, this would’ve absolutely warranted a recap if I’d been discussing my own wedding plans; however, the fact that the “conversation” happened at midnight should’ve tipped off Siri that this was a late-night binge session and not an actual conversation needing to be recapped.

Rather than coming away better informed about the vital conversations I’d had throughout the day, I came away feeling validated by the sheer chaos of it all. The constant whiplash of being pulled in a dozen different directions — bouncing between work, kids, gossip and the occasional sticky beverage crisis — was real and now immortalized (until the recap automatically expires if you don’t choose to save it).

It has been revealed that for now, while novel, neither Siri Recap nor Live Rewind is reason enough to buy (or avoid) the Apple Watch Series 12 or Ultra 4. They’re two of our top-rated smartwatches for their fitness, health and other smart features. Audio Intelligence is either an added bonus (it’s free) or something you can ignore altogether.

But if you do decide to venture into this brave upcoming world of AI notetakers, my suggestion would be to use Siri Recap intentionally rather than leaving it running all day.

Turn it on before a work meeting, a doctor’s appointment or another conversation where you might want a few notes to jog your memory later. Just make sure everyone involved knows it’s enabled and is comfortable with it, and that you’re not relying on it for crucial information.

If the stakes are high, have a backup — whether that’s your own notes or a recording — lest you risk coming home with the wrong kid.

📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Porch Pirates Don’t Care About Your Doorbell Camera. Follow This Expert Plan Now

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1264 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, doorbell cameras may seem like a good way to make a porch thief think twice, but the reality doesn’t quite match up.
  • That’s the case for my fellow CNET editor, Gael Cooper, who had her Amazon delivery stolen a few weeks ago and spotted the thief on camera.
  • Industry observers note that “When Amazon emailed me that the order was delivered and it wasn’t there, I was very confused,” Cooper remarked.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, doorbell cameras may seem like a good way to make a porch thief think twice, but the reality doesn’t quite match up. Some porch pirates don’t care about being caught on camera as long as they’re able to steal your package, and it’s unlikely that law enforcement will track down the stolen goods.

That’s the case for my fellow CNET editor, Gael Cooper, who had her Amazon delivery stolen a few weeks ago and spotted the thief on camera. It wasn’t expensive tech or a snazzy holiday gift — it was $36 worth of soda.

Industry observers note that “When Amazon emailed me that the order was delivered and it wasn’t there, I was very confused,” Cooper remarked. “When I pulled up the Ring footage, I saw the delivery happen on video, but then, 10 minutes later, a man in a blue hooded coat who’s intentionally hiding his face shows up and grabs the box.”.

It has been revealed that package theft cases like this happen year-round, with CNET findings showing that 28% of US adults have had a package stolen, know someone who has or have stopped an attempted theft. And experts predict more stolen packages during the holidays, when thieves expect more deliveries.

Sources indicate that so, don’t give thieves a chance. Now’s the time to make a proposal to keep your Black Friday and Cyber Monday packages out of sight. But what tactics actually work if doorbell cameras don’t? Here’s what you should know about porch piracy and how to lessen your chances of package theft.

It has been revealed that cooper’s Amazon order was scheduled to arrive between 3 a.m. and 6 a.m. — when it’s dark, but she knew she would be home. But thieves were already out lurking during those hours. Cooper noted the thief followed the driver and stole the package. She saw the thief stealing the package on her Ring security camera system.

Greg Zakowicz, Omnisend’s e-commerce and retail advisor, mentioned Cooper’s package-theft incident is fairly typical, unfortunately — especially during the holiday season.

“Thieves know as well as shoppers that orders increase during this time, and often, the packages are more likely to contain more valuable items,” stated Zakowicz. “Shoppers during this time look to take advantage of deep discounts for not only gifts but themselves, making the package a potential goldmine for thieves.”.

Industry observers note that there are a few steps you can take to lessen the likelihood of porch piracy. Zakowicz recommends using options like in-store pickups, post office boxes, in-garage delivery or deliveries to your workplace.

That advice is especially important for expensive tech you strategy to have delivered to your home unless someone will be there to grab the package immediately.

“While it may be less convenient, it’s a small price to pay to not have the hassle of gifts and expensive items going missing at the busiest shopping time of the year,” noted Zackowicz.

According to recent reports, also ask your retailers not to ship the item in the manufacturer’s packaging. Some retailers, like Amazon and Target, will clearly display this before shipping because it could be an easy hint for thieves to guess what it is — especially if it’s tech. Even though this won’t stop porch pirates from being curious about what’s in the box, it may make them think about the effort and risk versus the potential reward, Zakowicz said.

In a recent development, if you want another option to have packages delivered to your home, consider scheduling your deliveries for a time you know you’ll be available. For instance, you can set up an Amazon Day to have all of your Amazon packages delivered at once so you can proposal accordingly.

CNET found that US adults have mixed feelings about how effectively security cameras deter porch pirates: 11% of US adults believe they don’t deter them, while 9% use security cameras to get proof — not prevent it.

According to recent reports, regardless of your home security measures, don’t assume you’re safe from porch pirates just because you have a doorbell camera, and don’t use it as a means of keeping an eye on your package if you’re busy or not home. Instead, when you see motion detection, that’s a sign to grab it right away.

Industry observers note that “The most common misunderstanding is that having security cameras will prevent thieves from stealing packages,” stated Zakowicz. “Thieves are thieves because being caught is not their biggest worry. They also know porch piracy is not at the top of most officers’ day-to-day public service worries. Often, by the time the report is made, thieves are long gone.”.

It has been revealed that unfortunately, thieves may find other ways to steal packages, since their tactics are constantly changing. If that happens to you, there are a few steps you should take right away.

It has been revealed that file a police report of the incident first. Be prepared to share information, including a description of the thief, and the make and model of the vehicle, with the police and your community so they can be vigilant of the thief.

Industry observers note that but don’t get your hopes up that the thief will be caught. Zakowicz stated it’s rare that porch theft cases get solved.

Sources indicate that “Police aren’t necessarily dedicating resources to solving porch pirates who stole a new stuffed animal or board game. However, it’s important for them to understand areas seeing an uptick in thefts, as they can be more alert to suspicious activity,” noted Zakowicz. And the retailer may request it.

After filing, Zakowicz states to report the theft to the carrier and retailer. Carriers may use the data to assess future likelihood of package theft incidents and it could help instruct delivery drivers to carefully hide packages. Retailers may also be able to assist with a replacement.

Cooper filed a police report with her local police department, which allowed her to upload the Ring video of the theft and acknowledged receipt. She’s not expecting the thief to be caught, but figures that her report could possibly help in some way.

“I live in a pretty safe neighborhood in Amazon’s own hometown, but their delivery trucks are on our street dropping off packages every day,” she mentioned. “It’s got to be a banquet for hungry thieves.”.

She reached out to her neighbors to tell them about the theft, and one reported that she, too, had had a package stolen a week earlier.

Recent findings suggest that cooper says she did not intentionally choose the early-morning drop-off time, but it was the only time Amazon offered for her delivery. Since then, she’s seen Amazon try to offer that same time and has chosen not to order an item rather than be forced to use that dark, quiet delivery slot.

Recent findings suggest that immediately after the theft, Amazon was less than helpful, routing her to an AI agent who mentioned it understood the situation was upsetting but that it wouldn’t be able to do anything for four days. When she checked back, Amazon agreed to refund her for the item, but kept insisting on labeling the package as “missing” and asked her to report back if she “found” it.

Recent findings suggest that “I hope the driver doesn’t get in trouble for a supposedly ‘missing’ package,” she mentioned. “It unnerves me that she was being followed by a thief. Who knows how long he followed that truck and how many packages he scooped up?”.

    There have been ways to adjust the iPhone alarm volume for a few years, but there’s an important distinction between what the new feature entails and what those methods involve.

The newly introduced feature, however, lets you set an independent volume for all alarms and timers, not just those in the Sleep Schedule.

    Alarms, Timers, Alerts, and System Sounds are set to match your ringtone volume by default, but you can turn them off in the Sounds and Haptics setting.

    Also: 5 upcoming Apple Health features you should try in iOS 27.3 – if your phone qualifies.

    Once you disable the option to match your alarm volume to your ringtone’s volume, you can set your volume for upcoming alarms. With this feature, you can maximize your alarm volume without affecting the volume of incoming calls and notifications.

    #108228. Zelda Producers: Ocarina of Time Remake Is a Bridge to the Future

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1032 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

    Zelda Producers: Ocarina of Time Remake Is a Bridge to the Future

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1032 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Over the last month, I fell in love with a upcoming game that’s actually old.
    • Sources indicate that I’m still thinking about (and playing) Ocarina of Time on the Switch 2, even with GTA 6 loaded up at home.
    • I also can’t stop thinking about what a game like this means for Nintendo’s next wave of Switch 2 games, and a future Zelda game.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Over the last month, I fell in love with a upcoming game that’s actually old. It’s happened to me before, but Nintendo’s Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake drove that feeling home in a surprising way. How did Nintendo get me to fall so deeply in love again with a game I’ve already played? And why is it still winning me over, even with Grand Theft Auto 6 here?

    Sources indicate that I’m still thinking about (and playing) Ocarina of Time on the Switch 2, even with GTA 6 loaded up at home. GTA’s universe overwhelms me, but it also makes me appreciate Ocarina’s focus and clarity. And it’s also another incredible graphics showcase for what the Switch 2 is capable of. Yes, GTA 6 is jaw-dropping. But so are Ocarina’s 60fps vistas and details. Zelda pioneered 3D gaming before GTA ever went 3D.

    I also can’t stop thinking about what a game like this means for Nintendo’s next wave of Switch 2 games, and a future Zelda game. Zelda’s previous games became increasingly open world, full of multiplying tasks and larger maps. It can get overwhelming. Ocarina of Time’s focus is smaller, but still tangled and immersive. Can the two concepts feed off each other? Will Ocarina help rethink where the next Zeldas are heading? And, maybe, where other open-world games are heading, too?

    At Ocarina’s launch, I met in person with Nintendo’s producers for the remake, Eiji Aonuma and Hidemaro Fujibayashi, to discuss what it all meant and how the remake bridged the gap between the “old Zelda” and “newly introduced Zelda.” Aonuma has been a producer for Zelda games since the original Ocarina of Time, and Fujibayashi directed both Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom.

    For this project, they brought on staffers who’d worked on Tears of the Kingdom, many of them much younger developers.

    In a recent development, “In fact, some of them hadn’t even played the original Ocarina of Time on Nintendo 64,” says Aonuma. “We also saw this as a really interesting opportunity for this younger staff to make discoveries on the course of this project that they could bring forward on future Zelda projects that they might work on as well.”.

    There are a lot more subtle visual clues, I found, even than what I remembered in Nintendo’s last two Zelda games.

    According to recent reports, “When we were working on Tears of the Kingdom, we had this very high capacity to express all kinds of details and this feeling of immersion in the world, and that’s something I think was a big influence on the remake,” states Aonuma. “Whether it’s a visual detail that you might spot from a distance that you may not have in the original, that could be something that draws the player in and suddenly gives them the motivation to explore.”.

    What worked wonders, I found, was the quiet, subtle immersion, especially when exploring dungeons or figuring out solutions I’d forgotten decades ago. I had to study the environment for clues.

    That’s the magic ingredient: a throughline in the Zelda games that Fujibayashi says is “the idea of exploration and discovery.”.

    Fujibayashi appreciates how the visual tools have improved, even since Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom on the original Switch.

    According to recent reports, “A system that lets you share a high, dense volume of information visually provides upcoming ways of giving clues to the player: They can use their sight to gather the information they need to do some of the puzzle solving,” he says. “Even if you compare the graphics to Breath of the Wild, it looks slightly more realistic now. And that impacts how we approach puzzle solving and puzzle creation.”.

    I think about Grand Theft Auto as the newly introduced benchmark for immersion and graphic detail, but I’m also finding that a lot of GTA’s discoveries are made through pop-up interaction graphics that let you know when something can be activated. Ocarina of Time doesn’t always do this. And I also can’t help but wonder: Could the Switch 2 achieve a way to run a new wave of impressive games using optimized graphics, even something on a level like Grand Theft Auto’s latest?

    Or, rather, what if Nintendo aims for a newly introduced level of hyper-immersion in its games going forward, learning from Ocarina of Time?

    Sources indicate that speaking of immersion, I kind of wish I could hold my Joy-Con up and use it like an ocarina in the upcoming game. You can’t, although you can use the controllers to play notes or hum or play a tune into the built-in microphone using your own voice or instrument — something lots of people have been showing off online. But the Joy-Con-as-ocarina idea almost became a reality.

    According to recent reports, “To be honest, we did briefly think about doing exactly that, but then we also considered how difficult it is to turn the Joy-Con into something that’s going to make a sound that is faithful, and then also how to develop that into the application inside of the game as well,” says Aonuma. “What we ultimately decided to do instead was to have this audio recognition feature in the software where you can use any instrument that you would like, whether it’s analog or digital, and you can play these themes and have the effect in the game and experience that way.”.

    Sources indicate that what I’m really hoping for is a Majora’s Mask remake, the second N64 Zelda game that built off Ocarina’s graphics engine. Nintendo could do the same here, although Nintendo wouldn’t answer my questions about Majora’s Mask during my interview.

    I’m still unlocking all the little secrets in Ocarina of Time, sinking into the world as I go. And when I play the notes on my Switch, I imagine I’m playing that ocarina. After playing this Zelda game, I wonder what Nintendo could do with that same level of detail for Mario’s return on the Switch 2, almost 10 years after the last upcoming 3D Mario game on the Switch. We might know the answer to that soon enough.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Google has added Wallet integration to Personal Intelligence in AI Mode, letting you learn about your spending habits, plan a budget, maximize credit card rewards, and more with a simple Search.

    Industry observers note that starting today, Google confirmed, Personal Intelligence for Search is expanding to more apps, including Wallet and Drive. Google can’t move or manage any money, but it can give you tailored, personalized search results about your finances, like showing where you spend the most, identifying recurring subscriptions you might not be aware of, and suggesting which credit card might be best to use for travel. All you have to do is ask in a search.

    Also: I tried Personal Intelligence in Android Auto – and it knew exactly where I wanted to go.

    This feature comes just over a week after Google introduced Personal Intelligence to Wallet.

    Once your Wallet is connected, it takes a few minutes to fully sync. Once it’s finished, you can ask questions through AI mode in Search.

    I decided to give it a try for myself, starting off with a simple query: “Based on my spending, what’s a quick way I can save money?” I could have told you one of the primary culprits, but Google happily responded with what I already knew: far too much of my money goes to fast food and coffee.

    “You frequently grab quick-service meals,” the response said, pointing out several fast food places that I do indeed frequent, “and specialty coffees throughout the week.” If I just cut that down to two meals and two coffees a week, Gemini explained, I’d save about $30 a week, or $1,500 a year.

    Also: This powerful Gemini setting made my AI results way more personal and accurate.

    Sources indicate that when I asked it to find recurring subscriptions, Gemini noted that I had several monthly charges. What I didn’t ask for, but it did, was to break down those subscriptions into an easy-to-see chart, complete with the name, price, category, the card it’s being charged to, and the timeframe it usually comes out. Gemini even offered a few free alternatives to services I was paying for.

    It has been revealed that since Gemini also knows what cards are linked to your Wallet, it’s able to offer advice there, too. I’m planning a trip to Newly introduced York City, so I asked which cards might be best to use for the hotels and airfare. Gemini was able to analyze my card benefits, considering things like rewards and built-in travel insurance, and make a recommendation.

    Also: Slow Android phone? How to speed it back up in 4 easy steps.

    While Gemini Personal Intelligence can access your Gmail to learn more about your spending, it can’t access your bank account. The only information it knows about your finances and spending comes from receipts in your inbox or from your Wallet transaction history. I do use Wallet often (mostly when ordering through online apps), but it’s not quite my go-to option when I’m in a store. Given how useful this feature can be, though, I might just start using Wallet more to give it more information to work with.

    It has been revealed that spaceX has three segments, all in rapidly changing, revolutionary industries, so the organization could look very different in three years. Here's what could happen.

    SpaceX gets its name from its space business, which is the world's largest rocket-launching company. It works with private companies, as well as government agencies like NASA, and it brings satellites into space for its Starlink broadband business.

    In a recent development, the manufacturer measures its progress by debuts and mass to orbit in tons. It has already launched 113 rockets this year as of the end of the third quarter, sending 1,517 metric tonnes into space, and its business represents 90% of global mass to orbit. Revenue increased 6% year over year to $1.8 billion in the quarter, and it reported an operating profit last year but a $7 million loss this year. As it scales, it's likely to become reliably profitable.

    In a recent development, CEO Elon Musk announced a newly introduced base opening in Louisiana, set to launch in 2029. It's going to have 20 launch towers, and he expects it to launch thousands of rockets annually into space, bringing millions of tons of cargo. While there should be high capital expenditures to get it up and running, SpaceX just caught its first landing spaceship, and reusable rockets should dramatically lower its costs.

    According to recent reports, starlink is growing fast and highly profitable. It offers satellite broadband across the globe and right now covers 174 countries. It has more than 11,000 satellites in low earth orbit, and it plans on having 100,000, covering every area of the world, including lakes, oceans, and airplanes. It has 13.6 million customers as of the end of the third quarter, up from 12 million the year before, and it already has deals with many of the world's major airlines.

    Revenue increased 69% year over year to $5.2 billion in the third quarter, and operating income doubled to $2.4 billion.

    Recent findings suggest that the artificial intelligence (AI) business xAI merged with SpaceX earlier this year before the IPO, and the company renamed it Superintelligence (AI). It fits with the other segments because management expects to launch a million mini, solar-powered data center satellites into space, and AI is where management sees its biggest opportunities.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    According to recent reports, so far, it's growing fast. Revenue increased 830% year over year in the third quarter, but that included revenue from the acquisition of the coding organization Cursor, so growth may slow. Operating income swung from a $1.7 billion loss to $431 million.

    The manufacturer now has two huge data center clusters, Colossus I and II, with I fully rented to Anthropic. It has 1.7 gigawatts of power, and it expects to have 2.5 to 3 by the end of the year. Musk thinks it will have another 10 by the end of 2027, and possibly 20.

    It also has its own AI model, Grok, and its AI agent, Grok bot, of which Musk said, "I've never seen anything grow this fast.".

    Here's where it gets a bit tricky. Even if everything goes smoothly and SpaceX is much bigger in three years, its stock may not take off quite the same way. That's because it's already extremely expensive, trading at 55 times trailing 12-month sales. That kind of valuation isn't likely to last.

    Recent findings suggest that wall Street expects revenue to increase 272% in 2027, a major acceleration from the third quarter's 161%, and earnings per share of $0.34. Elon Musk said he thinks annual recurring revenue could reach $500 billion to $1 trillion next year, implying a much larger increase from today's $32.7 billion in trailing 12-month revenue.

    Regulations could also potentially change, slowing down AI development in general and impacting SpaceX.

    Let's suppose it can grow by a compound annual growth rate of 80% over the next three years. That would generate $190 billion in revenue over three years. At just under half of today's price-to-sales ratio, 25, the market cap would be $4.8 trillion, or about 260% higher than today's price.

    Gen Z is the least interested in AI at work – and it’s not even close

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, generation Z might have the lowest morale around AI at work compared to other generations.
    • Recent findings suggest that gen Z, which includes those born between 1997 and 2012, expressed the least interest and found the least utility in AI, Seramount found.
    • Also: OpenAI is offering small businesses free AI support – and up to $8K/mo to experts who help them.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, generation Z might have the lowest morale around AI at work compared to other generations. That’s according to a survey from talent services firm Seramount, which found that Gen Z was the most AI-averse among the generations surveyed about using the technology in their jobs.

    Recent findings suggest that gen Z, which includes those born between 1997 and 2012, expressed the least interest and found the least utility in AI, Seramount found. Only 18% of Gen Z reported an interest in strengthening their AI skills, compared to 36% of Millennials, 46% of Gen Xers, and 43% of Boomers. Gen Z is also using AI less than other generations, by nine percentage points.

    Also: OpenAI is offering small businesses free AI support – and up to $8K/mo to experts who help them.

    “Employers cannot assume their youngest employees will embrace AI on their own,” noted Diana Forster, senior director of research at Seramount.

    The survey polled responses from over 1,800 US white-collar workers at companies with at least 500 employees.

    Around half of Gen Z report weekly AI use (not specific to work), according to a survey from Walton Family Foundation, GSV Ventures and Gallup, but the generation’s skepticism has mounted over the past few years. Even members of Gen Z who use AI daily have less positive views on the technology. In the same study, 42% of Gen Z reported feeling anxious about AI in 2026, a 1% increase from 2025. Last year, 36% of Gen Z respondents reported excitement about AI. In 2026, that percentage dropped to 22%.

    Also: These companies are actually upskilling their workers for AI – here’s how they do it.

    It’s no surprise Gen Z is skeptical about adopting a technology that could be undermining their own career development. The labor market has been particularly harsh to this group of workers, as entry-level job postings have fallen in recent years, and many fear that AI will only exacerbate unemployment. Around 8% of those ages 22 to 24 were unemployed in September, compared to 3% of workers ages 25 to 54, according to data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics.

    But with many workplaces still adopting AI, senior employees are trying to prepare Gen Z by getting them on board at work.

    “We need to show young workers how AI can strengthen their work, provide clear guidelines and training, and give them opportunities to practice using it and build the skills they’ll need as leaders,” Forster mentioned.

    • The music streaming app declared on Tuesday that it is banning all tracks it determines to be entirely AI-generated.
    • The app also said distributors, such as DistroKid, TuneCore, CD Baby and others, would not be allowed to deliver wholly AI-generated music.
    • According to Tidal, 43% of tracks distributed to the app over the past three months were completely AI-generated, including 60% of the music submitted on Nov.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The flood is too much for Tidal. The music streaming app declared on Tuesday that it is banning all tracks it determines to be entirely AI-generated. The platform said it’s making the move after being increasingly inundated with non-human music. As of Dec. 9, Tidal will no longer accept or host fully AI-generated tracks.

    The app also said distributors, such as DistroKid, TuneCore, CD Baby and others, would not be allowed to deliver wholly AI-generated music.

    According to Tidal, 43% of tracks distributed to the app over the past three months were completely AI-generated, including 60% of the music submitted on Nov. 6 alone. Tidal mentioned the affected tracks were labeled as AI and removed from the royalty pool, which is the pot of subscription and ad revenue paid out to rights holders.

    Before Tuesday’s action, Tidal had tried to lessen AI’s influence by identifying, labeling and demonetizing AI tracks, as outlined in its AI policy. But amid the growing influx of AI music, representatives for the app mentioned it was time for “a more drastic change.”.

    Recent findings suggest that tidal noted there are 27 million tracks in its catalog that are 100% AI, but 96% of them have not been streamed at all in the past three months. Those 27 million tracks make up 6.3% of Tidal’s entire listings.

    The firm has removed more than 65,000 tracks flagged for artist-name impersonation.

    It has been revealed that some AI help is permitted. Musical tracks where the maker used AI assistance but did not rely on it to generate the entire track will be allowed on the platform. Tidal uses ⁠Ircam Amplify to detect AI.

    A Tidal representative told CNET that the app does not set a maximum amount of AI assistance that can be used to make tracks, and affirmed that only tracks that are deemed 100% AI-generated would be removed.

    In a recent development, read more: I Only Listened to AI Music for a Week. It Was Terrible, but Not for the Reason You Think.

    In a recent development, “Tidal will always fight for artists to get paid more,” the firm stated in its announcement. “Everything in this upgrade comes back to that. If you make music, you should be able to put it on Tidal knowing it won’t be buried under tracks no one asked for or copied by someone pretending to be you.”.

    Generating music with AI is increasingly easy with online tools. The AI song-generation platform Suno can create songs using only text prompts. With Google’s Lyria, you can use photos or text prompts to generate tracks up to 3 minutes long.

    In a recent development, AI music also is not just about creating hit songs. Some industries need affordable music for short-form videos, games, apps and retail spaces, and they are increasingly turning to AI to supply it.

    But streaming apps and other companies are fighting back against AI slop, which refers to often poor-quality AI-generated social media posts, articles, music, videos and images inundating the internet in an attempt to generate click-and-stream revenue.

    It has been revealed that youTube recently rolled out a latest labeling system to indicate which music is AI-generated. Deezer provides a free tool listeners can use to see which tracks are AI-generated. Spotify is labeling which musicians are AI and which are human. Apple is flagging AI-generated music so listeners can spot it.

    You can turn Claude artifacts into Windows and Mac apps now – here’s how

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (659 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Anthropic is making its Claude artifacts available as desktop apps, meaning you can share and more easily access your most-repeated tasks on your computer.
    • Also: 4 ways Anthropic’s Claude Sheets beat using a Google Sheets connector.
    • Industry observers note that anthropic first released artifacts in 2024.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Anthropic is making its Claude artifacts available as desktop apps, meaning you can share and more easily access your most-repeated tasks on your computer. The “install as app” feature is available in beta for all free and paid Claude plans and works on both Mac and Windows, but not Linux.

    Also: 4 ways Anthropic’s Claude Sheets beat using a Google Sheets connector.

    Industry observers note that anthropic first released artifacts in 2024. Since then, they’ve become a way to standardize and repeat tasks users do regularly, especially at work. Previously, artifacts ran via your Claude window or in a browser. By splicing them out as distinct desktop apps, you can now run different Claude queries while also using your artifacts locally, or use those apps without opening Claude at all.

    Recent findings suggest that “When an artifact is installed as a Mac or Windows app, it gets its own icon and opens in its own window instead of inside Claude. You can share it with others, and it needs your permission before it can interact with your computer,” Anthropic mentioned.

    Artifact apps can still access Claude and any connectors you’re using, and they patch automatically when you edit the artifact itself in Claude. When apps request something from Claude, though, that goes toward your Claude usage limits, which are lowest for free people.

    Anthropic remarked the app feature is meant to streamline building apps for both developer and non-developer work.

    Also: Can AI plan terrorist attacks? US tested ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok.

    Sources indicate that the patch clarifies where AI software for work is headed. Claude is already more of an AI-powered work suite than a single helpful chatbot for many organizations. Evidently, people are using tools like artifacts frequently enough — and simultaneously with other Claude features — that they need those Claude-based tools to function like discrete bits of software on their own.

    “If you rely on a tool for work, it should open like the rest of your apps and remind you when something needs your attention,” Anthropic remarked.

    It has been revealed that claude artifact apps don’t have the same functionality as apps you could build using Claude Code, though. Even if you don’t need Claude open for these apps to work, you’ll still need to be signed in to Claude and have internet access, so they’re not an entirely portable or off-grid option.

    The feature’s support page also notes that legacy artifacts, “live artifacts from Claude Cowork,” and artifacts generated from templates like Docs, Slides, and Sheets can’t be installed as desktop apps.

    It has been revealed that first, make sure Claude for Mac or Windows is updated. You can try the “install as app” feature, which is in beta for all free and paid intends, via Claude’s Share menu. Select the Install as app option, which will then download the artifact you chose to your desktop. From there, set permissions as needed.

    Permissions range from the default (whatever they are in a browser) to app-specific permissions like sending notifications and full computer access.

    Also: I tried replacing Claude Code with a local AI stack that’s completely free.

    Industry observers note that full computer access means the artifact app can “run programs and read, change, or delete your files without asking each time,” Anthropic remarked, so proceed carefully. Every time you edit and enhancement the artifact (and thus the app), Claude will ask you to confirm permissions again, so you’ll ideally have regular checkpoints to revise access. Still, there are some guardrails in place: Anthropic only lets you give full computer access to apps you’ve made yourself. For Team and Enterprise intends, that extends to any apps made by your coworkers.

    “Anthropic doesn’t review apps before you install them, so only give full access to apps you trust,” the manufacturer remarked.

    For Claude Enterprise prepares, the install-as-app feature is off entirely until an admin turns it on in Organization settings.

    Breaking: I Tried Using Meta Muse and ChatGPT Dots to Save on Groceries. They’re Not Quite There Yet

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1187 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that high grocery prices have been in the news for years now.
    • So before you drop a fortune on gas and drive out to the grocery store to spend even more on sustenance in your prep for hosting or bringing dishes to your holiday celebrations, you might consider using an AI agent to find you the best deal possible.
    • Recent findings suggest that although, in my experience, it’s not as simple as the AI marketing makes it sound.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that high grocery prices have been in the news for years now. The cost of eggs, how much you’re paying for a bowl of cereal and whether or not meat is back on the menu are the recurring subjects of nationwide headlines.

    So before you drop a fortune on gas and drive out to the grocery store to spend even more on sustenance in your prep for hosting or bringing dishes to your holiday celebrations, you might consider using an AI agent to find you the best deal possible.

    Recent findings suggest that although, in my experience, it’s not as simple as the AI marketing makes it sound. Here’s what happened when I tried to use AI agents to find the lowest possible prices on groceries.

    AI agents such as Meta Muse and ChatGPT’s Dots can only crawl so many sites and online fliers for prices. Some stores and e-commerce sites have blocked AI agents from accessing their URLs. The first step in finding cheaper groceries with AI agents is to check which sites and stores they can access for price comparisons.

    Where both agents missed a step was in the limitations they put on their searches, at first only looking at the retailers I had shown via my receipts and a few other big-name grocery stores.

    I clarified in the chats and in a 20-minute voice conversation with Muse and a 14-minute voice conversation with Dots that they should expand their horizons and look at discount online retailers like Martie.com, and check what they could around advertised pricing and offerings at local farmers’ markets.

    Muse stuck to the basics like Ralphs, Target and Walmart, and then expanded to Sprouts, Vons and Martie.com when prompted.

    After further nudging, Muse also reviewed user-reported pricing from Costco (I don’t have a membership), gave me vague information about Grocery Outlet, suggested Misfits Market/Imperfect Foods, ruled out Amazon Fresh and gave me some sample pricing from a local butcher for meats.

    Muse also checked some local bakery prices after I mentioned I’d like to find alternatives to sweet treats at a more affordable price.

    Dots checked all the usual places that Meta Muse checked with a few extras thrown in — Smart & Final for produce, meat and some packaged products, and Super King’s monthly ad.

    Industry observers note that neither of the tools checked Trader Joe’s. Muse mentioned that the grocery chain doesn’t show prices of its products online, despite me finding that the Trader Joe’s website indicates prices of its products online. Both Dots and Muse admitted to only checking the local store’s pages when asked.

    Sources indicate that you could spend some time making a list from scratch of all the groceries you might need every two weeks and give that list to the AI agent for its search. You could also skip all that and take some pics of your most recent grocery receipts and online payments and have the AI agent build the list itself.

    According to recent reports, I had some receipts saved, and the AI agents I used for this test were able to put together an accurate grocery list from them. I also provided emails showing receipts from online orders of household items and groceries for the past month to build my orders.

    Muse took my receipts and concluded that, surprise, surprise, shopping at Gelson’s was not as cost-effective as shopping at Walmart. It spat out a lot of specific information about comparisons on some of the items in my list, but completely ignored others.

    Dots looked over my receipts and recommended I try shopping at Super King for most fresh meat, produce and a few grains, and keep Walmart as my main option for packaged products like pasta sauce.

    Both tools tackled this task in a way I was not expecting — as a narrative exploration of my overall grocery spending, with generalized suggestions supported by specific examples of spot pricing.

    It was kind of like they’ve been optimized to write essays about grocery shopping as a school assignment, and not to be agentic personal assistants for real-world work.

    Maybe it was the way I phrased the task, but I was hoping to get an actual shopping list with price comparisons for each item, or at least equivalent items, and a guide on where and how to procure said items.

    Neither AI agent provided this autonomously and had to be directly prompted to provide grocery lists in response to a very specific request.

    It has been revealed that AI agents are supposed to be pros at anticipating the needs of their human bosses. I was keen to see how the always-on AI agents would handle managing the recurring needs of a small household and if they might make any autonomous suggestions meant to save me money in ways I hadn’t anticipated.

    At no point did Muse seem to be actually thinking outside the strict parameters of the review of the items on the receipts I sent. This felt more like a conversation about what I’d previously purchased with a side serving of attempts to get me to connect Instacart to the tool.

    It was also the most confusing grocery shopping experience I have ever had. That might be on me, but I would assume the agent might ask some questions, like how often I usually shop, what my monthly budget for groceries is, and how many people and animals live in the house. Muse didn’t ask any of those things and had to be prompted consistently.

    Muse sent me the final grocery list as a raw Markdown file, which was hilarious. I got a .pdf version after explicitly asking for one.

    Industry observers note that my original total with one in-person shop and one online order was about $180. Muse’s total with three in-person shops and one online order came in at around $153.

    Dots was slightly better suited to this task after some prodding, and gave me some options for building prep meals with low-effort, high-protein recipes based on how I usually shop.

    According to recent reports, dots’ final grocery list included everything I asked for, but still missed some key items, like solid substitutes for pricey prepped foods. Dot’s final total with two in-person shopping trips and a whole lot of missing items came out to around $85.

    Industry observers note that this test reinforced my findings about how agentic AI tools tackle domestic or traditionally invisible labor tasks. In my limited use cases so far, they are about as useful as a loose dog turd tumbling around in a clothes dryer.

    If you’re not looking to book a flight and hotel for a business conference in Philadelphia or put your Sweetgreen order on autopilot, the AI agents exhibit a startling lack of curiosity and autonomous thinking.

    In a recent development, there’s still a large gap in common sense on the part of agentic AI for those of us hoping these tools will make our everyday lives outside of a 9-to-5 easier, more affordable or less hectic. I hope that changes as they learn.

    By Rich Smith – Nov 25, 2026 at 1:03PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Urban Outfitters ›.

    Urban Outfitters (URBN -10.33%) stock tumbled 12.1% through 12:40 p.m. ET Wednesday despite beating (barely) on Q3 earnings last night.

    Recent findings suggest that heading into the report, analysts expected Urban Outfitters to earn $1.52 per share on $1.67 billion in quarterly sales. As it turned out, Urban Outfitters earned $1.54 per share, while sales met the consensus.

    In a recent development, that hardly seems like the kind of results to spark a 12% sell-off! And yet it did. So what went wrong?

    Industry observers note that brand by brand, growth was weakest at Anthropologie, responsible for 40% of sales -- but sales there inched up only 3.2%. The namesake Urban Outfitters brand grew its sales 4.6%. FP Group ("Free People") saw the briskest sales growth -- a whopping 14.6%, contributing most of the growth for the quarter.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    Anthropologie's relatively weak performance appears to underlie today's falling share price. Commenting on the results last night, Morgan Stanley analyst Alex Straton complained that she had hoped to see recent "green shoots" at Anthropologie sprout into much bigger sales than actually materialized in Q3.

    With "Anthro improvement increasingly necessary to unlock investor appreciation of the broader portfolio's value," notes Straton -- and that improvement taking longer to arrive -- the worry now is that investors may have to buckle down and prepare to endure "Anthro's more prolonged deterioration.".

    With analysts now anticipating Urban Outfitters will grow earnings only about 5% annually over the next five years, even a relatively modest 13x price-to-earnings ratio may not be cheap enough to make Urban Outfitters stock a buy.

    #108207. The FCC Approved a Million SpaceX Satellites for Data Centers in Space

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (606 w)

    The FCC Approved a Million SpaceX Satellites for Data Centers in Space

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (606 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Federal Communications Commission has approved SpaceX’s request to launch 1 million AI-equipped satellites to create vast data centers in space.
    • SpaceX initially filed an application in May asking for permission to launch the satellites, collectively known as Starmind.
    • Recent findings suggest that “It’s just really abrogating their responsibility to go, ‘Well, this is a project they’re proposing.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Federal Communications Commission has approved SpaceX’s request to launch 1 million AI-equipped satellites to create vast data centers in space.

    SpaceX initially filed an application in May asking for permission to launch the satellites, collectively known as Starmind. The FCC’s approval requires that SpaceX launch its first data center satellite by 2030 and meet the 1 million mark by 2040.

    Recent findings suggest that “It’s just really abrogating their responsibility to go, ‘Well, this is a project they’re proposing. Is this actually safe?’” Jonathan McDowell, an astrophysicist who tracks satellite introduces, told CNET. “It’s a blank check. Launch as many satellites as you can, and we’ll just see what happens. I think this is a mistake on the FCC’s part.”.

    Orbital data centers have long been a goal of SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, becoming a pivotal part of his pitch to investors ahead of the organization’s IPO in June.

    In a recent development, “You’re power-constrained on Earth. Space has the advantage that it’s always sunny,” Musk said in March.

    On its web page for Starmind, SpaceX touts its high-efficiency solar arrays on the planned satellites and the cooling benefits of space. It says that high-speed laser links will beam the AI results back to Earth through Starlink’s constellation.

    Space experts I’ve talked to this year about Starmind have been skeptical. The technical challenges alone are dizzying; the scale of SpaceX’s ambitions is hard to swallow.

    Industry observers note that it’s taken seven years for Starlink to grow its constellation to 11,195 satellites, and that was already an unprecedented feat. Is it possible to get to 1 million satellites in 14 years?

    Industry observers note that “We do not have the launch capacity for any of this,” Ian Christensen, senior director at the Secure World Foundation, told me in a previous interview. “Not even within SpaceX to do their own constellation, let alone the other constellations planned.”.

    Industry observers note that spaceX has increasingly prioritized launching its own satellites instead of letting commercial customers hitch a ride on their rockets. Starlink’s share of SpaceX missions has gone from 54% of its Falcon 9 rocket’s missions in 2020 to about 79% in 2026, according to a Reuters analysis. One analysis estimates that SpaceX would have to launch 5,000 Starship rockets a year to meet its goal — a staggering increase from 330 rockets that launched last year in total.

    Industry observers note that scientists have already been ringing alarm bells about overcrowded orbits as they exist now. The more satellites in space, the more difficult it is for operators to maneuver around each other. A single crash could turn into decades of orbital debris, which could cause a chain reaction that eventually makes space inoperable for everyone. And burning up all those satellites in the atmosphere when they reach the end of their lives has already started to leave ozone-depleting aluminum particles behind. A paper published this week in Earth and Space Chemistry estimated that SpaceX’s data center strategy would multiply pollutants in the upper atmosphere by more than 150 times compared to last year.

    “There are scientific papers out there raising concerns,” McDowell said. “Yes, they’re unproven, but if I say, ‘Yeah, we’re not sure if this is going to destroy the atmosphere and kill us all, but it might,’ is the right reaction to go, ‘Well, you haven’t proven it, so we’re just going to ignore it’?”.

    The FCC’s approval came despite objections from Amazon, the environmental nonprofit Public Employees for Environmental Responsibility and the American Astronomical Society.

    A representative for SpaceX did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

    Can AI make Thanksgiving less painful?

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (996 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mashable

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that I have a liberal friend who I was talking with the other day about plans for Thanksgiving.
    • Sources indicate that "I’m dreading it," he remarked.
    • Every November, we all pretend that turkey, stuffing, and pumpkin pie are worth being trapped by three generations of relatives you barely know.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that I have a liberal friend who I was talking with the other day about plans for Thanksgiving. He’s going home to his family in Oklahoma, who are anything but liberal.

    Sources indicate that "I’m dreading it," he remarked. "My uncle sits in a chair watching Fox News on his phone, and my great-aunt will try to tell me in so many ways, without telling me, that I’m going to hell for being gay.".

    Every November, we all pretend that turkey, stuffing, and pumpkin pie are worth being trapped by three generations of relatives you barely know. Just call me the Grinch of Thanksgiving.

    Recent findings suggest that sure, not all of us are in an inhospitable environment like that, but for many, it's as awkward as waving back at someone on the street who was actually waving at the person behind you. When the atmosphere is heavy, with everyone waiting for the proverbial shoe to drop, it inevitably does — loudly, like a construction boot.

    Years ago, with a former partner’s parents, the mother dropped her fork, pointed across the table at me, and noted in Spanish, "I can’t look at him." It was all downhill from there.

    It has been revealed that back in the day, before technology swallowed us whole and gave us hunched necks, surviving Thanksgiving required biting your tongue, heavy drinking — though that often fueled the fires of ferocity — or staying away. Your only defenses were hiding in the bathroom, taking a long nap, or pretending to be a die-hard Detroit Lions fan (they traditionally play every Thanksgiving), eyes and ears glued to the TV to tune out the bickering.

    Industry observers note that if you wanted to fact-check a wild political claim your uncle blurted out, you just had to let him win because you couldn’t pull the truth up on your phone. If you needed a sounding board before walking into the lion's den, you had to psych yourself up alone, and rehearse answers in your car at the end of the driveway.

    Sources indicate that this year, however, things look different. Lately, we’ve spent plenty of time worrying about how artificial intelligence is taking over the internet and creeping into our daily routines. It is everywhere now. There’s no arguing that fact with your uncle.

    According to recent reports, yet one of its most underrated perks is acting as a real-time social buffer. AI has quietly become an infinitely patient wingman sitting right in your pocket, ready to keep your holiday civil, lighthearted, and blissfully brief on drama.

    In a recent development, think about the dread before you even walk through the front door. Just thinking about harrowing Thanksgivings past sends a chill down my spine, and I wonder how different they might have been with a little help. Now, on the drive over, you can open a chatbot and treat it like a life coach.

    According to recent reports, give it the persona of your most relentless relative, say, a Fox News-addicted uncle, and practice your responses to off-the-wall questions. Doing a two-minute dry run gets the awkwardness out of your system before you ring the doorbell. I tested this with Claude, feeding it a list of potential landmines, and got back sharp, diplomatic ways to deflect and make light of the moment.

    I won’t share them here, but I encourage you to do your own.

    In a recent development, for instance, what if a real-time brouhaha erupts at the table? Instead of letting two relatives shout until everyone is quietly burping into their napkins, whip out a voice-mode AI assistant to act as a neutral referee and break the logjam.

    In a recent development, if you are hosting, the stress starts even earlier. Seating arrangements require more diplomacy than a UN General Assembly, and pairing the wrong two cousins guarantees a tug-of-war over the mashed potatoes. Feed your guest list and everyone's friction points into an AI tool, and ask it to build a seating chart that separates natural adversaries with at least two buffers, a centerpiece, or a spot at the kids’ table. (I was single for many years, so that’s where I always ended up.).

    You can even have AI generate a custom trivia game to steer conversations away from danger zones like politics, Donald Trump, whether AI will kill us — don’t ask AI about that — or whether the new John Madden movie on Amazon is actually bad or just quirky.

    It has been revealed that finally, tension often starts days earlier in the chaotic family group chat, sparked by passive-aggressive comments about who brings what. Instead of firing back a reply you’ll regret on Thursday, paste the thread into an AI assistant and ask it to translate your annoyance into something warm, firm, and drama-free.

    Obviously, AI cannot fix deep family dynamics, and it won't miraculously turn my friend’s Oklahoma relatives into MS Now viewers. Still, I told my friend to load up his chatbot before his flight. Between his Fox News uncle and his judgmental great-aunt, having a calm digital wingman in his pocket might be the closest thing he gets to a Thanksgiving miracle.

    By Adam Spatacco – Nov 25, 2026 at 1:15PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

    Industry observers note that the last several weeks have been unusually volatile for Nvidia (NVDA -3.91%) investors. Between the departure and subsequent reinstatement of founder Jensen Huang as CEO and growing concerns surrounding an artificial intelligence (AI) bubble, investors have had plenty to digest.

    It has been revealed that while much of the discussion around Nvidia focuses on its leadership and the unprecedented demand for data center infrastructure, another potential catalyst is hiding in plain sight. Interestingly, Nvidia stock could generate multibagger returns over the next year without the tech giant exceeding Wall Street's growth expectations.

    Let's explore why valuation expansion could be the biggest catalyst for Nvidia stock as 2027 approaches.

    Recent findings suggest that during the third quarter of fiscal 2027 (ended Oct. 25), Nvidia's revenue surged 103% year over year to $115.8 billion. Meanwhile, adjusted earnings per share (EPS) increased by 111%. Management raised its fiscal 2028 revenue growth outlook from 70% to 75%.

    According to recent reports, despite Nvidia's accelerating growth, shares are trading at a steep discount to their all-time high. Moreover, Wall Street analysts currently forecast Nvidia to generate $16.48 in EPS next fiscal year, implying a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple of 8.8 based on a current share price of $146.

    NVDA EPS Diluted (TTM) data by YCharts.

    Recent findings suggest that although Nvidia's earnings are overwhelmingly driven by its data center business, the firm's valuation is influenced by several other factors. These include competition from Advanced Micro Devices and custom chip designs from Broadcom as well as macro factors like rising interest rates. These variables are impacting investor confidence in the sustainability of Nvidia's profits.

    According to recent reports, nvidia's compressed valuation suggests investors are skeptical about the durability of the company's earnings power. However, several developments could change that perception throughout next year.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    One of Nvidia's most underappreciated opportunities revolves around its software ecosystem. Between CUDA, Nvidia AI Enterprise, and its Nemotron family of open-weight models, the firm is becoming increasingly embedded in how AI developers build and deploy applications.

    Investors shouldn't necessarily focus on the amount of software revenue Nvidia generates today. Instead, it's important to understand how Nvidia is using software to make its chip empire more indispensable. As developers remain tied to both Nvidia hardware and software, the tech giant is in a position to strengthen customer retention and increase switching costs. This should alleviate concerns that Nvidia's competitive advantage will erode as alternative chip architectures come to market.

    Another catalyst is Nvidia's capital return strategy. In September, the company's board authorized an additional $150 billion in share repurchases, leaving approximately $227.3 billion available under its buyback program at the end of the third quarter. Even if net income remains constant, a reduction in outstanding shares can still increase EPS.

    One of the most compelling aspects of Nvidia's current valuation profile is that the firm doesn't necessarily need to exceed Wall Street's earnings expectations for the stock to appreciate. The table below illustrates how different valuation multiples would influence Nvidia's share price, assuming fiscal 2028 EPS remains constant at $16.48.

    The big takeaway here is that Nvidia stock could more than double if investors are willing to assign the company a multiple of 20 times projected fiscal 2028 earnings. Even a relatively modest expansion to 15 times earnings would imply roughly 68% upside.

    In a recent development, investors may be overlooking how much pessimism is already reflected in Nvidia's stock price. Should the firm simply meet existing expectations while demonstrating disciplined capital allocation and the durability of its competitive moat, Wall Street could gradually re-rate what Nvidia's earnings are worth.

    Ultimately, Nvidia's next rally may have less to do with how much money the company makes and more to do with how much investors are willing to pay for those profits.
