    Etihad’s Upcoming Credit Cards Are Primarily for Status Chasers

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1272 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, etihad Guest, the loyalty program of Abu Dhabi-based Etihad Airways, is expanding its U.S.
    • It has been revealed that the two cards are the Etihad Guest Visa Signature® Card ($99 annual fee) and the Etihad Guest Premier Visa Signature® Card ($499 annual fee).
    • They also offer extra miles on international transactions (neither has foreign transaction fees) and purchases with Etihad’s partner airlines, which include U.S.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, etihad Guest, the loyalty program of Abu Dhabi-based Etihad Airways, is expanding its U.S. presence by introducing two latest credit cards. Most people won’t get much value from these cards, but they can make sense for Etihad frequent flyers who want elite status.

    It has been revealed that the two cards are the Etihad Guest Visa Signature® Card ($99 annual fee) and the Etihad Guest Premier Visa Signature® Card ($499 annual fee). Issued by the First National Bank of Omaha, both offer faster pathways to earning and maintaining elite status and the ability to earn extra miles on Etihad purchases.

    They also offer extra miles on international transactions (neither has foreign transaction fees) and purchases with Etihad’s partner airlines, which include U.S. carriers like American Airlines and JetBlue Airways.

    Here’s what you need to know about the cards.

    The Etihad Guest Visa Signature® Card comes with a $99 annual fee, and it earns Etihad Guest miles at the following rates:.

    3 miles per $1 spent on Etihad purchases.

    2 miles per $1 spent on Etihad partner airline purchases.

    2 miles per $1 spent on non-U.S. purchases.

    1 mile per $1 spent on all other U.S. purchases.

    According to recent reports, welcome offer: Through Feb. 3, 2027, the card is offering the following welcome offer for latest applicants: Earn up to 40,000 welcome Etihad Guest Miles, including 10,000 miles after the first purchase and an additional 30,000 miles after spending $3,000 within the first three billing cycles after account opening.

    Elite status benefits: You’ll also get Etihad Silver status after your first Etihad purchase within 90 days of opening your account. Unlike most airlines, that entry-level status is enough to get you into the business class lounge when traveling through Etihad’s hub at Abu Dhabi’s Zayed International Airport.

    You can retain that status by spending $20,000 a year on the card, or $3,000 a year on Etihad purchases.

    The Etihad Guest Premier Visa Signature® Card comes with a $499 annual fee, and it earns Etihad Guest miles at the following rates:.

    5 miles per $1 spent on Etihad purchases.

    3 miles per $1 spent on Etihad partner airline purchases.

    2 miles per $1 spent on non-U.S. purchases.

    In a recent development, 1 mile per $1 spent on all other U.S. purchases.

    The only differences in rewards between the premium and standard cards are increased earning rates for eligible airline purchases.

    According to recent reports, welcome offer: Through Feb. 3, 2027, the premium card offers a higher welcome offer compared to the standard card: Earn up to 60,000 welcome Etihad Guest Miles, including 20,000 miles after the first purchase and 40,000 miles after spending $7,000 within the first three billing cycles after account opening.

    Elite status benefits: The premium card offers a faster track to elite status: automatic Silver status upon card approval and Gold status after your first Etihad purchase within 90 days of opening your account.

    In a recent development, to maintain Gold status, you’ll need to spend $40,000 a year on the card, or $8,000 on Etihad purchases. Otherwise, you’ll have Silver status.

    Wi-Fi benefit: After your first Etihad purchase, you’ll get 3,000 Etihad Guest miles, enough to cover Wi-Fi costs on a long-haul Etihad flight. You’ll then get those miles again after each cardholder anniversary.

    Travel benefits: The card offers a statement credit for Global Entry or TSA PreCheck and select travel protections. If you already have a premium travel card, you might already have access to these perks.

    Sources indicate that the card also includes a Priority Pass lounge access membership. However, an Etihad spokesperson told NerdWallet that it’s the entry-level membership tier, so you’ll need to pay for yourself and guests each time you visit a Priority Pass lounge. Most premium credit cards in the U.S. that offer Priority Pass allow complimentary visits for at least the cardholder.

    The Etihad cards make the most sense for Etihad’s frequent flyers who are flying to or connecting through Abu Dhabi several times a year.

    That’s because the standard card’s accelerated pathway to Etihad Guest’s Silver status tier can unlock the ability to choose business class lounge access in Abu Dhabi as a status perk.

    According to recent reports, with the premium card, you get a fast track to Gold. If you select lounge access as a Gold status perk, you can not only bring a guest on the same flight into the lounge, but also access Etihad’s worldwide lounge network. That includes Etihad’s own lounges in New York and Washington, D.C., as well as most partner lounges at other Etihad destinations.

    According to recent reports, bear in mind that while Etihad has many partnerships with other airlines, it’s not part of an alliance, so you don’t get lounge benefits when traveling on partners. You’ll need to be flying on an Etihad-operated flight to get into the lounge.

    If you primarily fly with other carriers, then Etihad status will have limited upside for you.

    In a recent development, however, the Priority Pass lounge membership that comes with the premium card does not have that restriction. You can access Priority Pass lounges while flying on any airline, although you’ll need to pay an additional per-person $35 fee each visit.

    In a recent development, the earning rates on the Etihad cards are lackluster for everyday spenders. The bonus categories are for airline purchases with Etihad and its partners, as well as international spending.

    That means your day-to-day purchases at home, like groceries, dining out and gas, earn only 1 mile per $1 spent.

    Plus, there are more ways to earn Etihad Guest miles than spending on an Etihad credit card. For example, you can transfer points to Etihad Guest from Bilt Rewards, Capital One and Citi ThankYou.

    Those programs offer cards that typically have better benefits and bonus categories, and they offer flexibility on how you can use your points and miles. With an Etihad card, you can only earn Etihad Guest miles, which expire after 18 months without qualifying flight activity. (If you’re not traveling on Etihad or its partners at least once every 18 months, then you definitely should not get the cards.).

    One of the most interesting perks of the new cards is the bonus category for spending with Etihad partner airlines — 2 miles per $1 for the standard card and 3 miles per $1 for the premium version. Typically, airline credit cards reward customers only for spending on the airline, not partners.

    There are better cards available, though. Some offer as many or even more points per $1 on flights purchased directly from airlines.

    If you want the card solely to earn more Etihad Guest miles, then the answer for most people is no.

    While you can earn more miles for purchases with Etihad and partner airlines, the earning rates aren’t attractive enough to justify the annual fees, especially when compared with existing cards with currencies that transfer to Etihad Guest.

    Status chasers could benefit from the fast track to elite status — but you would need to be a fairly frequent Etihad flyer to really take advantage of your elite benefits.

    You want a travel credit card that prioritizes what’s crucial to you. Here are some of the best travel credit cards of 2026:.

    Flexibility, point transfers and a large bonus: Chase Sapphire Preferred® Card.

    No annual fee: Wells Fargo Autograph® Card.

    Flat-rate travel rewards: Capital One Venture Rewards Credit Card.

    Bonus travel rewards and high-end perks: Chase Sapphire Reserve®.

    Luxury perks: American Express Platinum Card®.

    Business travelers: Ink Business Preferred® Credit Card.

    Addas a preferred source on Google.

    In a recent development, health insurer UnitedHealth delivered better-than-expected results for the third quarter of 2026. The tech giant also raised its full-year earnings outlook, reflecting continued progress on its turnaround blueprint.

"UNH's beat & raise reinforces turnaround momentum, with improving MA [Medicare Advantage]/Optum Health supporting a higher '26 EPS baseline & upside to '27 consensus," stated Wright.

    Furthermore, Wright highlighted management's view that the consensus 2027 EPS of $22.63 was too conservative. Reaching even the low end of the tech giant's 13% to 16% long-term EPS growth target would imply an EPS of $23.17.

    Wright raised her 2026 EPS estimate to $20.65 from $19.82 and 2027 EPS to $23.24 from $22.54, reflecting the latest upside and an improving 2026 medical loss ratio to 87.4% from 88.1%.     Industry observers note that wright ranks No. 264 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. Her ratings have been successful 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 15%. See UnitedHealth Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    Social media giant Meta Platforms has been making headlines since the launch of its Muse AI agent, which is seeing solid traction. Investors look forward to updates on the company's AI strategy when it introduces its third-quarter results on Oct. 21.

    It has been revealed that heading into Q3 earnings, Guggenheim analyst Michael Morris maintained a buy rating on Meta stock and increased his price target to $850 from $700, reflecting higher estimates for 2027. He expects Muse usage momentum and engagement levels to shape investor sentiment into the Q3 earnings call.

    Specifically, Morris highlighted that, according to Apptopia, Muse reached 1.3 million daily active consumers in five weeks versus 300,000 in the first week. Given that Muse's current adoption represents less than 0.05% of Meta's 3.6 billion daily active user base, the analyst expects management to prioritize boosting usage over near-term monetization.

    "Over time, we believe Muse monetizes primarily through businesses paying to reach consumers through their agents, consistent with the economics of Meta's core advertising business, rather than consumer wallets," remarked the five-star analyst. He added that the checkout integrations with Shopify and PayPal reflect this framework.

    While there are concerns that a rival could overtake Muse or the recently rolled out Muse Wonder and push Meta into a prolonged cycle of overinvestment, Morris remains bullish due to the company's strong record in scaling WhatsApp and competing strongly with TikTok via Reels as well as free distribution to an extensive user base.

    After hosting a non-deal roadshow with Marvell's senior management following the Investor Day, Stifel analyst Tore Svanberg reiterated a buy rating on the stock with a price target of $370.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Courtney Carlsen – Nov 25, 2026 at 1:15PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than X-Energy ›.

    Hyperscalers face a substantial question: How do you feed power-hungry data centers while working toward net-zero carbon emissions? Amazon (AMZN -3.14%) is betting nuclear energy can help bridge that gap. The company is backing 5 gigawatts of new nuclear power by 2039, with small modular reactor developer X-energy (XE -4.75%) playing a key role.

    In a recent development, with projects in the pipeline, Amazon's partnership gives X-energy a powerful backer and an opportunity to prove its nuclear technology can deliver. Could the artificial intelligence (AI) boom help turn this next-generation nuclear stock into a major growth opportunity?

    In 2019, Amazon co-founded The Climate Pledge, which calls on signatories to reach net-zero carbon emissions by 2040. More recently, Amazon laid out prepares to cut the carbon intensity of operations by 65% compared with 2019 levels.

    A major component of Amazon's carbon-reduction goals involves nuclear energy, which provides carbon-free, reliable, 24/7 baseload power that data centers desperately need. Nuclear energy complements intermittent renewables, like wind and solar power, and numerous hyperscalers, including Microsoft, Meta Platforms, and Alphabet, are signing agreements for nuclear power.

    In a recent development, amazon launched its $2 billion Climate Pledge Fund in 2020, and it used some of those funds to become an early investor in X-energy in October 2024 during its Series C-1 financing round. Amazon provided much-needed project and development funds, and has been central in helping X-energy with the design, licensing, and build-out of its nuclear fuel facility.

    According to recent reports, X-energy develops the Xe-100 SMR, a high-temperature, gas-cooled nuclear reactor. The Xe-100 uses small graphite pebbles packed with uranium particles and coated in a high-temperature ceramic, and it uses helium gas for cooling. The reactor uses its core physics and heat-resistant fuel to naturally shut down the nuclear reaction and passively dissipate heat without pumps or human intervention.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    In a recent development, SMRs are appealing because they are manufactured in modular factory units and can be linked together. For example, each Xe-100 produces 80 megawatts (MW) of electricity and can be linked together, like the 12-unit, 960 MW project planned in Indiana.

    Amazon has been crucial for X-energy, helping it fund a four-unit project totaling 320 MW with Energy Northwest in central Washington. It has also committed funding to develop the 12-unit project with American Electric Power at the former coal plant in Indiana. Meanwhile, X-energy's project with Dow in Texas has cleared regulatory review for construction and hopes to deliver power by the early 2030s.

    Sources indicate that SMRs could completely change how we think about and deploy nuclear energy, and X-energy is one of many start-ups in the space. Amazon has helped X-energy clear regulatory hurdles and secure commercial agreements, giving it a massive leg up on competitors that lack similar backing.

    In a recent development, X-energy could be a massive winner over the next decade as the nuclear renaissance unfolds. That said, X-energy's story is still being written, and it will be several years before it deploys its first reactors commercially, making the stock best suited for your watch list for now.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A reconditioning fee is an added dealer charge you might find when buying a used car. It’s intended to cover any costs the dealer incurs to make sure a used car is showroom-ready, from mechanical inspections to detailing.

    The reconditioning process varies between dealerships, but typically includes these steps:.

    In a recent development, A visual exterior inspection. An auto tech does a quick walk-around the vehicle and notes any corrosion, damage or wear.

    Recent findings suggest that an interior inspection. The engine and auto interior are examined and tested, and any issues are documented.

    Recent findings suggest that A test drive. The car is taken out for a drive to check that it runs well and that the radio, brakes, A/C and other components are all functioning properly.

    In a recent development, service and repair. Any interior or exterior mechanical, functional or cosmetic complications that were found are repaired, including paint, dents, oil changes and major engine work.

    It has been revealed that inspection. Once repairs are completed, the car is inspected again to make sure everything looks and functions as it should.

    Sources indicate that detailing. This includes deep interior, engine and exterior cleaning as well as any necessary leather refurbishing, bumper repair or wheel restoration.

    Reconditioning fees are legal, but that doesn’t mean you have to pay them. Dealers can charge whatever they want for a reconditioning fee, and it’s not uncommon to find them ranging from around $500 to over $2,000.

    The good news: Reconditioning fees, like most dealer extras, can be negotiable. Ask the dealer for a breakdown of the reconditioning fee to see what kind of work was done to prepare the car for sale. If the work was minor but the fee is high — for example, if they’re asking for $1,995 but replaced the floor mats only — that’s a good sign it’s a bogus charge.

    According to recent reports, however, when it comes time for negotiation, don’t just haggle over the reconditioning fee or other individual fees. The best way to negotiate is to focus on the out-the-door price, or the total amount you’re paying for the car. This simplifies the negotiation process and keeps you focused on the true price of your car.

    All dealers invest some amount in reconditioning, but those costs are often built into the dealer’s asking price for a vehicle, rather than as a separate charge.

    Recent findings suggest that some dealers opt to add a reconditioning fee to the bill because it allows them to advertise a lower asking price online, which doesn’t include fees. It’s a tactic to get you into their dealership, since the asking price is lower than that of other dealerships.

    However, once you arrive, you may find that the out-the-door price is the same — or more — compared with what other dealers are asking.

    Some car-buying experts recommend avoiding dealerships that charge reconditioning fees altogether. But remember that the out-the-door price is what matters at the end of the day, so it’s worth comparing prices at multiple dealerships to find the best deal.

    Industry observers note that reddit is an online forum where owners share their thoughts in “threads” on various topics. The popular site includes plenty of discussion on financial subjects like car buying, so we sifted through Reddit threads to get a sense of how users feel about reconditioning fees. People post anonymously, so we cannot confirm their individual experiences or circumstances.

    According to recent reports, reddit customers are generally skeptical toward reconditioning fees. Many users view these fees as a bait-and-switch tactic: dealers advertise an attractive price online and then tack on the fee at the dealership, inflating the actual out-the-door cost well above what was listed. Car buyers frequently share stories of being hit with reconditioning fees ranging from a few hundred dollars up to $2,000 or more, often with little or no evidence of what work was actually done.

    Car-buying experts on Reddit point out that most dealerships already build reconditioning costs into the sticker price, so if the fee is listed separately, the dealership may be double-dipping. Several customers suggest that car buyers ask their dealer for an itemized breakdown of the work done, but most users recommend negotiating the total out-the-door price rather than individual fees.

    10 stocks we like better than BYD ›.

    The global automotive market is shifting as electric vehicles challenge traditional engines. Investors must decide if high-growth BYD (BYDDF -2.40%) or the established legacy of General Motors (GM +2.03%) offers a better path forward.

    Sources indicate that BYD focuses on new-energy vehicles, batteries, and rail transit, establishing itself as a leader in the transition away from fossil fuels. General Motors relies on its massive scale and profit-heavy internal combustion engine sales to fund its own electric transformation. Both are competing for dominance in a rapidly changing transportation landscape.

    Sources indicate that BYD is a prominent player in the global automotive industry, which is a major part of consumer discretionary stocks. The firm designs and sells newly introduced-energy vehicles while also operating in electronics, batteries, and rail transit systems. Its footprint covers more than 400 cities worldwide, supported by a massive workforce of nearly 869,622 employees.

    In a recent development, in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached about $120.4 billion. The manufacturer reported a net income of approximately $4.7 billion during this time frame. Revenue growth was roughly negative 4.5% compared to the prior twelve-month period, reflecting recent shifts in the global market.

    In a recent development, as of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was nearly 0.7x. This ratio compares total debt to shareholder equity to show how a company funds its operations. Its current ratio, which measures the ability to cover short-term debts with short-term assets, was approximately 0.8x. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was nearly negative $14.6 billion, representing the cash remaining after the business covers its day-to-day operations and capital equipment.

    General Motors designs and builds a wide variety of trucks, crossovers, and cars, supported by more than 10,000 authorized dealerships globally. The firm maintains strategic joint ventures for battery production and vehicle sales, particularly in the Chinese market. It also operates a captive finance arm to provide financing options for customers and dealers.

    In a recent development, in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue was about $187 billion. Net income for the period was approximately $4.0 billion. This represented a revenue growth rate of nearly negative 0.3% as the company navigates the transition to new technology.

    Sources indicate that as of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio reached roughly 2.1x. This metric indicates the relationship between total debt and shareholders' equity. The current ratio was close to 1.2x, representing the tech giant's short-term liquidity. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow reached approximately $11.1 billion.

    According to recent reports, BYD faces significant challenges due to geopolitical trade tensions, as many regions are considering or imposing tariffs on imported vehicles. The company also operates in a crowded Chinese market where price wars can weigh on financial results. Furthermore, its global expansion requires significant capital investment in diverse regulatory environments.

    General Motors faces risks in executing its long-term electric vehicle strategy, especially if consumer adoption remains slower than anticipated. The company also faces significant regulatory risks, including recent $220 million settlements related to customer data privacy. Additionally, operations are sensitive to supply chain disruptions and the financial performance of international joint ventures.

    General Motors appears to be the more conservatively priced option, as it carries a lower multiple of both earnings estimates and sales.

    Valuation metrics include those sourced from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from those of other data providers.

    Industry observers note that general Motors has had a decent year, widening its market share in the U.S. to more than 17%, to stay the biggest car seller in the country. Also, hybrids like the Chevy Equinox and Blazer and the EV Cadillac Lyriq have been better sellers than expected, calming some fears that GM was falling behind in the trend toward hybrids and EVs.

    In a recent development, the firm has also been aggressively buying back shares, which supports the share price in the market and makes profitability appear to be improving on the per-share level. GM also shifted its shares to the Nasdaq Stock Market recently to try and get itself listed on the Nasdaq 100 index, which would also be supportive for shares, given that about $1.4 trillion in assets are indexed to the Nasdaq 100. The company is also lauded on Wall Street for handling the various Trump tariff issues that had generated fears the business would be adversely impacted.

    That remarked, top-line growth is slow, with 2027 revenue seen rising $3 billion to $189 billion and net income exceeding $12 billion, up from about $9 billion expected for full year 2026.

    Turning to BYD, while the tech giant doesn't have a U.S. presence, it is one of the top automakers in China. The automaker's September vehicle sales increased about 17% compared to the same month in 2025, headlined by a remarkable 154% jump in overseas shipments of passenger vehicles and pickups. It's part of the company's goal of catching Toyota Motor Co. (TM +2.77%) as the world's largest automaker. Overseas sales were about 39% of BYD's sales in the third quarter. Yet it has its domestic challenges, with Q3 China sales declining more than 18% for BYD, due to intense pricing competition and a hurting Chinese consumer.

    Still, foreign sales should help BYD push 2027 sales up 16% in its reporting currency of Chinese yuan, to about $145 billion at today's exchange rate.

    According to recent reports, so which stock to go with? BYD's push into Europe appears to be going very well, but that is counterbalanced by domestic problems. GM is a bargain price at a forward P/E ratio of 5.8x. The Great Recession bailout by the U.S. federal government revealed how important GM is to the U.S. economy. The bet here is that GM's leading position in the world's second-largest car market, the U.S., will continue to hold, and management will continue to find ways to improve returns to shareholders.

The bulk carrier order book, however, now stands nearly at 15% of the existing fleet, which is up from around 13% at the time of our last call, mainly due to heavy Capesize and Newcastlemax fleet ordering, which now represents 23% of the existing fleet. 13% of the Kamsarmax and Panamax fleet is on order and 15% of the Ultramax/Supramax fleet is still on order. Ship recycling remains extremely low. According to BIMCO, only 70 bulkers of 3 million tonne deadweight in total were recycled between January and October.

    This is 36% lower year-on-year, the lowest level in 18 years, and it confirms that the 5 million tonne deadweight of scrapping, which was expected at the beginning of the year will not be reached. And then to finalize Slide 18. Let's conclude with the main positive and negative factors that analysts expect could influence the dry bulk market going forward. On the positive side, ton-mile demand remains supportive with 2026 growth forecast at 4.1%, above projected fleet growth of 3.9%. Long-haul Atlantic to Asia iron ore and bauxite trades continue to support Capesize and Newcastlemax utilization. Grain exports from the Americas and selected trade routing will help Panamax and geared vessel employment.

    Industry observers note that operating speeds will remain at near historical lows while dry docking and geopolitical disruption absorbs effective capacity and demolition is expected to remain limited, but the aging fleet and firm recycling prices could, at some point, provide medium-term scrapping potential. On the negative side, fleet growth is expected to accelerate in 2026, especially for Capes. BIMCO forecast 2027 supply growth of 3% to 4% against demand growth of 0.5% to 2.5%, depending on whether and how long the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed. Chinese steel output is declining, which could weigh on iron ore demand, while China's coal imports have started to soften on high inventories.

    Policy risk, especially in Guinea, where export controls are expected to slow bauxite shipments as well as in China and Indonesia. Geopolitical uncertainty remains high, prolonged high energy prices could hurt global growth and a reopening of the Strait of Hormuz or a full return to the Red Sea would release tonnage and shorten trade routes. And on this note, I will pass the call back to our CEO, Ms. Semiramis Paliou, for some notable takeaway points from this earnings call. Thank you very much.

    What Are Repositioning Cruises?

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1042 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, A repositioning cruise is a one-way sailing that moves a ship from one region to another.
    • Repositioning cruises are most common in spring (roughly March to May) and fall (roughly September to November), though they can occur at other times of year.
    • In a recent development, because ships are crossing oceans, these trips often include many days at sea.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, A repositioning cruise is a one-way sailing that moves a ship from one region to another. For example, many ships sail in the Mediterranean Sea during the summer and move to the Caribbean Sea for the winter, and that trip between the two is a repositioning cruise.

    Repositioning cruises are most common in spring (roughly March to May) and fall (roughly September to November), though they can occur at other times of year.

    In a recent development, because ships are crossing oceans, these trips often include many days at sea. For some travelers, that’s a chance to relax and enjoy the ship’s onboard amenities. Sometimes, these sailings can also be cheaper than traditional cruises.

    In a recent development, one key consideration for a repositioning cruise is that the embarkation and disembarkation ports will be different. This means you generally can’t buy a standard round-trip flight to and from the same city. Instead, you’ll need transportation to where the cruise starts and another way home from where it ends, which usually means two one-way flights (or one open-jaw ticket) unless you live near one of the ports. While these one-way sailings may be more affordable than traditional cruises, airfare costs may be higher.

    This could be a great opportunity to redeem miles for your flight.

    Another feature that sets these cruises apart is that stops along the way tend to include ports that aren’t traditionally part of regular itineraries. These might include islands like Bermuda, the Azores or the Canary Islands, and on some northern routes, Greenland.

    Just keep in mind that the main purpose of these sailings is to get to a new region for the next season’s itineraries rather than make daily port stops. So if you’re someone who wants to visit as many places as possible on a cruise, a repositioning sailing may not be the ideal choice.

    Repositioning cruises are often longer than standard cruises, commonly running two to three weeks compared with about a week for a typical sailing, which may appeal to travelers looking for an extended vacation. The experience is often more relaxed, with many days at sea and less of a rush to book shore excursions or visit crucial sites when off the ship.

    It has been revealed that if there are particular ships with certain amenities — like tattoo parlors or massive waterparks — that you really want to experience, keep in mind that not all ships reposition between regions. Some stay in certain regions year-round.

    Sources indicate that for ships that do change locations for the season, there are plenty of onboard activities to fill the time. You can enjoy highlights, food and wine tastings, organized activities and time at the spa, pool or casino.

    Many repositioning crossings are relatively smooth, and modern ships use stabilizers to reduce movement. But since these itineraries cross open ocean rather than staying closer to land, there can be more motion, especially on North Atlantic crossings in fall and winter.

    In a recent development, if you tend to get seasick, this could be a dealbreaker. Even if a repositioning sailing is smooth, temperatures can be chilly on the open ocean, especially on northerly or spring and fall transatlantic routes, with strong winds that may make suntanning by the pool less appealing.

    You can book one of these sailings in the same way you would book a traditional cruise. But if you’re searching for dates and itineraries on a cruise line’s website, they may be listed as transatlantic, transpacific or Panama Canal sailings rather than repositioning cruises, though some lines do use the term "repositioning." There’s even a website that specializes in rounding up these cruises: RepoCruises.com.

    Keep an eye out for themed sailings that focus on topics like wine, theater or music, where fellow guests on the ship may share similar interests. Cruise lines often schedule them on repositioning cruises to spur demand.

    Here are some repositioning cruises for 2027. They often take place during shoulder seasons, between the most popular cruising times in places like the Mediterranean or Caribbean.

    Recent findings suggest that this journey repositions the ship from Miami, where it sails on Caribbean itineraries, to Seattle, where it will visit ports in Alaska during the spring and summer months. Departing April 8, 2027, the 18-night cruise includes stops at various ports in Colombia, Panama and Mexico, as well as San Diego and Los Angeles, before arriving in Seattle on April 26.

    Regent Seven Seas Cruises' all-suite luxury ship Seven Seas Mariner will sail between Newly introduced York and Lisbon, making stops in Canada, Morocco and the Portuguese islands of Madeira and the Azores.

    Departing April 29, 2027, the 16-night journey ends in Lisbon, Portugal, as the ship repositions to Europe, where it will sail various itineraries, including Mediterranean sailings later in the summer season.

    Recent findings suggest that departing Seattle on Sept. 28, 2027, Norwegian Jade will sail to Yokohama, Japan, with stops in Alaska and northern Japan. This is a way to travel across the Pacific with less jet lag, since the journey takes place over several days, with ship clocks typically adjusted gradually (often an hour at a time) during the sailing. Note that the voyage also crosses the International Date Line.

    If Greenland has been on your bucket list, this 16-night sailing is a way to get up close and personal with its natural scenery. Departing Reykjavik on Aug. 25, 2027, Azamara Quest will sail from Iceland to the U.S. It will make stops in Greenland, Canada and Upcoming England before reaching the Big Apple.

    Departing Bergen, Norway, on June 11, 2027, this 28-night sailing aboard Viking Vela sails around Iceland's coast, makes two stops in Greenland and crosses the Atlantic before reaching Fresh York.

    • According to recent reports, shares of virtualization software firm Nutanix (NTNX -15.19%) plunged 17.7% on Wednesday as of 1:24 p.m.
    • Nutanix released its fiscal first-quarter 2027 earnings last night, exceeding expectations.
    • The CEO transition, combined with some imperfections in key underlying metrics and a bearish market mood, conspired to drive today's significant sell-off.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Billy Duberstein – Nov 25, 2026 at 1:28PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Nutanix ›.

    According to recent reports, shares of virtualization software firm Nutanix (NTNX -15.19%) plunged 17.7% on Wednesday as of 1:24 p.m. EDT.

    Nutanix released its fiscal first-quarter 2027 earnings last night, exceeding expectations. However, the company also revealed that its current CEO is stepping down, a move that surprised investors.

    The CEO transition, combined with some imperfections in key underlying metrics and a bearish market mood, conspired to drive today's significant sell-off.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    According to recent reports, in the first fiscal quarter, Nutanix's revenue increased 15.2% to $772.4 million, while adjusted (non-GAAP) earnings per share grew 78.0% to $0.73. Both figures beat analysts' expectations.

    Nevertheless, there were some imperfections in the quarter and in forward guidance. Management forecast a decline in the organization's operating margin in the fiscal year ahead, even as it raised the figure from its prior guidance. According to management, the company is going to invest more heavily in research and development and salespeople, in what it described as a "significant" reinvestment into AI and agentic capabilities.

    It has been revealed that additionally, the manufacturer's bookings, which reflect the value of total deals that have yet to be converted to revenue, fell 2% from the year-ago quarter. While management chalked this up to just a few large delayed deals and the company allocating resources differently, investors were in an unforgiving mood.

    Finally, CEO Rajiv Ramaswami announced he would step down from the position he has held for about six years and would stay on to help appoint his successor, ensuring a smooth transition. While this seems like an orderly CEO transition and has nothing to do with performance challenges or other concerns, the uncertainty about Nutanix’s leadership augmented all the other worries.

    The large investment behind agentic applications, the slight decrease in bookings, and the CEO transition weren't necessarily bright red flags that anything is wrong with Nutanix. However, the combination of all these factors, along with the extremely bearish sentiment toward tech stocks today, conspired to cause the big drop in Nutanix stock.

    In a recent development, this sell-off may very well be overdone, making today's drop a buying opportunity. Nutanix stock now trades at under 20 times this year's projected adjusted earnings per share. The firm has a healthy cash balance on its balance sheet, and its virtualization software is likely to remain in demand as enterprises manage data across public and private clouds.

    However, this underlying uncertainty may remain until Nutanix finally lands a fresh CEO, which could take months.

Mortgage lenders' rates are never identical, but when we're seeing rapid change, the gaps between lenders tend to widen — and that's for sure what I saw. I looked at six different lenders, and saw a nearly 70-basis-point difference between the highest and lowest APRs. (And yes, that was looking for the same loan amount, location and so on.).

    My point is, whether you're looking to buy or refinance, make sure to shop multiple lenders. You're the same candidate bringing the same financials to each one, but you could end up with extremely different rate quotes. And it pays to compare. Freddie Mac estimates that comparing at least two lenders could save you up to $600 per year in interest. Compare four or more, and that savings is over $1,200 annually.

    Here are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for context. For more, keep reading below the charts.

    » Take the next step: Compare mortgage rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

    Mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to new inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

    Mortgage rates may be lower today, but like I mentioned above, it's been more of a seesaw than a ski slope — and we may be about to hit the high side again. The latest Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index is due out tomorrow morning. Recently, when rates have moved higher, inflation's been in the mix.

    It has been revealed that strong inflation's generally bad for borrowing, including to buy a home, because higher interest rates are the remedy. Raising the federal funds rate (the short-term borrowing rate the central bankers of the Federal Reserve actually set) is the Fed's main tactic for managing inflation. While the Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, its decisions influence the entire economy. That includes mortgage lenders, who tend to adjust rates ahead of its decisions.

    We already know how PCE's likely to go, since it's the last of the three big inflation measures to be released. We've already gotten last month's Consumer Price Index and Producer Price Index. October's CPI came in worse than predicted, showing widespread price increases. (When most of the increase is driven by one area, it's easier to be optimistic that inflation can be contained.) And October’s PPI demonstrated wholesale inflation climbed at its fastest pace in almost four years. PPI measures the price businesses pay for things, so it's often a preview of what consumers could face once those costs get passed along.

    Predictions for October PCE aren't great, so at this point the hope is that the numbers aren't even worse than expected. And again, PCE's out tomorrow morning. We'll know whether we're getting seconds (actually, thirds) of bad October inflation news well before the turkey hits the table on Thursday.

    Industry observers note that markets are right now anticipating a quarter-point hike at the Fed's December meeting. Even though that'll remain the most likely outcome, a poor showing from PCE could spark speculation about a half-point hike. That probably won't be good for mortgage rates.

    Industry observers note that but back to the upcoming holiday: Markets will be closed on Thanksgiving, and Black Friday's a half day, so we'll all have a bit of a break this week. Mortgage rates don't move much when the markets aren't moving. I won't be here to talk to you about mortgage rates, either, 'cause NerdWallet gives us Thursday and Friday off. Happy Thanksgiving!

    » Learn more: How the Fed affects mortgage rates.

    Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you blueprint to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

    With rates where they are right now, you could start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.63% or higher — but there just aren't too many people for whom that's true.

    Also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

    If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

    Sources indicate that » Time to refi? Compare refinance rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

    There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.

    If the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

    NerdWallet’s affordability calculator can help you estimate your potential monthly payment. If a newly introduced home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. Not only will this free up more cash flow for a future mortgage payment, it can also get you a better interest rate when you’re ready to buy.

    » Is now a good time to buy? See NerdWallet’s analysis.

    If you already have a quote you’re happy with, you should consider locking your mortgage rate, especially if your lender offers a float-down option. A float-down lets you take advantage of a better rate if the market drops during your lock period.

    Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.

    🤓 Nerdy Reminder: Rates can change daily, and even hourly. If you’re happy with the deal you have, it’s okay to commit.

    » Stay informed: Check out NerdWallet's mortgage news hub for all our latest coverage.

    The rate you see advertised is a sample rate — usually for a borrower with perfect credit, making a massive down payment, and paying for mortgage points. That won't match every buyer's circumstances.

    In addition to market factors outside of your control, your customized quote depends on your:.

    Even two people with similar credit scores might get different rates, depending on their overall financial profiles.

    » Get the best rate for you: How to get the best mortgage rate.

    Maybe — but even personalized rate quotes can change until you lock. That’s because lenders adjust pricing multiple times a day in response to market changes.

    #108187. Breaking: The CEO's AI Blind Spot: Who's Really In Control?

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (922 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: The CEO's AI Blind Spot: Who's Really In Control?

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (922 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Travis McGregor is CEO and Co-Founder of SLC Digital, a hardware-rooted transaction assurance platform helping enterprises combat AI fraud.
    • In a recent development, ​Most CEOs have treated AI governance as a technology matter, something to delegate to the CIO, the security team or the vendor.
    • Industry observers note that once a system acts, someone has to answer for what it does.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Travis McGregor is CEO and Co-Founder of SLC Digital, a hardware-rooted transaction assurance platform helping enterprises combat AI fraud.

    In a recent development, ​Most CEOs have treated AI governance as a technology matter, something to delegate to the CIO, the security team or the vendor. That made sense when AI was primarily drafting emails and summarizing reports. But as AI systems take on greater responsibility—from approving payments to accessing sensitive records and acting on behalf of employees and customers—organizations need to do more than understand what these systems can do. They need to know which actions are authorized, who approved them and under what conditions.

    Industry observers note that once a system acts, someone has to answer for what it does. That responsibility sits with executive leadership, and many organizations are unprepared. According to Grant Thornton’s April 2026 AI Impact Survey, 78% of senior business leaders lacked strong confidence that their organization could pass an independent AI governance audit within 90 days. Three in four boards have approved major AI investments, but only 52% have set clear governance expectations.

    According to recent reports, throughout my career in the mobile industry, I’ve watched latest technologies advance faster than the infrastructure needed to support and secure them. AI is following that same pattern, but the stakes are considerably higher.

    I think of AI sovereignty as an organization’s ability to keep meaningful control over its AI systems, including where data lives, how models and agents behave, how information moves among vendors and who can authorize what those systems do.

    Three gaps tend to erode that control.

    Permissions are often granted broadly when a system is deployed, then left untouched as its responsibilities grow. An agent set up to draft vendor correspondence could eventually gain access to payment workflows. Access and authorization are different things, and a high-risk action deserves its own approval.

    Recent findings suggest that agents frequently work through existing credentials and enterprise workflows. When an agent uses an employee’s delegated access, a valid session alone may not establish whether a specific action reflected genuine human intent or exceeded the authority originally granted.

    Many companies have AI policies on paper with little visibility into whether those policies are enforced, especially across third-party vendors, cloud infrastructure and the wider AI supply chain.

    CEOs don’t need to design authentication systems or manage individual permissions. They do need to set expectations for control, oversight and accountability. That means deciding what AI systems can access, which decisions they can make alone and which actions require explicit human authorization. Those are judgments about risk tolerance, and they belong at the top.

    In a recent development, A governance policy offers little protection if an organization cannot demonstrate that its controls are being enforced. The CEO’s role is to set the limits and demand evidence that they are working.

    Recent findings suggest that as regulatory scrutiny of AI-driven decisions grows, organizations that cannot trace authorization chains may face greater compliance and liability risks. Counterparties are likely to follow. Just as proof of security controls became standard in enterprise vendor reviews, evidence of verifiable AI authorization may become an increasingly key part of due diligence.

    Adversaries are already moving. Deepfakes, voice cloning and synthetic identities are live threats today. Cyber-enabled fraud accounted for more than $17.7 billion in losses reported to the FBI in 2025. The bureau also recorded more than 22,000 complaints involving AI, with reported losses exceeding $893 million. Microsoft’s Digital Defense Report 2025 likewise documents how AI has accelerated fraud and impersonation techniques, including automated phishing. Workflows that rely mainly on behavioral inference to confirm who is acting may be particularly vulnerable to manipulation.

    In a recent development, the least visible risk may be operational. An AI system can work exactly as designed and still cause harm if it holds broader permissions than anyone intended, initiating actions no one explicitly approved.

    For each high-stakes AI decision affecting a customer, transaction or regulated asset, leadership should be able to say who authorized it, what permissions were granted and whether the action stayed within bounds. If answering those questions requires a forensic investigation, the organization may lack sufficient visibility into its AI systems.

    Identify the workflows where an AI recommendation, an authenticated session or a standing permission shouldn’t be sufficient on its own, and require stronger, verifiable authorization for those actions.

    Look past price and performance. Ask who controls the data, where processing happens, how information flows through third- and fourth-party relationships and how permissions are enforced. Jurisdiction, recovery procedures and accountability must also be part of vendor oversight.

    Activity logs can show what happened, but may not establish whether an action was explicitly permitted. Require systems to preserve evidence of identity, permissions, authorization and execution for high-risk actions, including cryptographically verifiable records where appropriate.

    AI is moving from a tool that helps people make decisions to one that can act on their behalf. That shift demands a different kind of oversight, one that goes beyond policies, permissions and vendor agreements to establish whether consequential actions were actually authorized.

    The organizations that get this right will be better positioned to adopt AI with confidence, knowing they can enforce boundaries, demonstrate accountability and maintain control as these systems become more autonomous.

    For CEOs, the real test of AI leadership is no longer how quickly their organizations can deploy the technology, but whether they can maintain control over what it does next.​.

    Forbes Technology Council is an invitation-only community for world-class CIOs, CTOs and technology executives. Do I qualify?

    10 stocks we like better than Space Exploration Technologies ›.

    Checking in to see what the billionaire hedge fund managers do is a smart investment strategy. While you shouldn't blindly follow all their moves, using them for idea generation is a smart plan.

    One billionaire hedge fund I follow is Appaloosa Management, run by David Tepper. During Q3, he loaded up on Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX +1.30%) shares. He owned barely any at the end of Q2 (SpaceX went public right before Q2 ended), but as of the end of Q3, it was the fourth-largest position in his portfolio, accounting for nearly 8% of its value. That shows extreme confidence in the stock, but should you follow suit and open a position in it?

    Recent findings suggest that one major reason retail investors should not blindly copy the moves of billionaire hedge fund managers is that the information we are getting is well out of date by the time we see it. Investment fund managers only have to report their end-of-quarter holdings in their 13F filings, so the purchases involved could have happened at any time during a quarter. And those forms don’t get filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission until 45 days after the quarter they cover has ended. So any given stock move described in those forms could be more than four months old by the time news of it reaches the general public.

    According to recent reports, during Q3, SpaceX traded as low as $110 per share and as high as $160 per share at the start of the quarter. It ended the quarter around $151 per share — just above its opening-day first trading price. Today's price of about $130 per share is right in the middle of the Q3 range where Tepper could have bought. So investors don't have to worry too much about overpaying for the stock, as it's on sale relative to where it traded for most of Q3.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    Additionally, by waiting to buy until now, you have more information than Tepper had available in Q3, and that information is quite bullish.

    Although SpaceX is generally recognized as a space exploration firm, it's increasingly an artificial intelligence investment. Its AI segment now accounts for over half of its revenue, and has grown at a 213% pace year over year last quarter. That's an impressive growth rate, and according to CEO Elon Musk, it's only going to get better.

    Industry observers note that during the Q3 conference call, Musk asserted that SpaceX's annual recurring revenue could rise to somewhere in the $500 billion to $1 trillion range by the end of next year, thanks to its booming AI division. While Musk is no stranger to making bold projections that don't always pan out, the bigger idea here is that there will be monster AI growth in 2027 that investors need to prepare for. With SpaceX becoming more AI-focused, I think it's a smart pick in this space.

    Recent findings suggest that investors should take advantage of the current price of SpaceX's stock and scoop up shares. Tepper may have been a bit early to the party by buying shares in Q3, but I think his decision was the right one.

    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nerdwallet ↗ Open Full Page

    How to Get Grants for College

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1054 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, grants are one of the best ways you can pay for your education.
    • In a recent development, grants can be used for tuition, course materials and other cost-of-attendance expenses.
    • Here’s how to use a college grant and what it can pay for.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, grants are one of the best ways you can pay for your education. It’s free money you aren’t expected to pay back.

    In a recent development, grants can be used for tuition, course materials and other cost-of-attendance expenses. Some grants, depending on who awards them, require an application or have requirements you must meet before you can get your money.

    Here’s how to use a college grant and what it can pay for.

    There are four main types of grants:.

    Federal grants come from the federal government.

    State grants come from state programs and often can only be used at schools in that state.

    Institutional grants come from your college or university, or even your program or major.

    Private grants come from nonprofits, community organizations and individual donors.

    In a recent development, to receive a federal grant, you must complete the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA). Most states require the FAFSA for state grants, and a few require a separate state application. You’ll need to complete the FAFSA for each year you’re enrolled in school. You may need to meet certain eligibility requirements, such as income limits, to get some grants. The FAFSA is how you apply for the Pell Grant, which is a financial need-based grant. The FAFSA also determines eligibility for federal work-study, which is a job program rather than a grant.

    Federal aid, including federal grants, typically requires students to meet satisfactory academic progress. This means you have to maintain a minimum grade point average and be on track to finish your degree on time, as determined by your school. Your school also sets how many credits you must take to qualify for grant funding.

    Some grants — typically private or institutional grants — require an additional application that asks for transcripts, letters of recommendation and personal essays. Your school’s financial aid office or the grant provider will have details on applying for specific grants.

    In a recent development, after you submit the FAFSA, you’ll receive a financial aid award letter from each school you applied to, which outlines how much in federal, state and institutional grants you’ve been offered. You must accept your aid to receive it.

    Most grants will be disbursed directly to your college or university. Your school will apply the grant money first to tuition, fees and any other charges it bills, such as housing or a meal blueprint.

    Sources indicate that in some cases, you may receive more grant money than your school bills, which is the best-case scenario. If that happens to you, any leftover funds will likely be refunded to you. Refund timelines vary by school, so it may take some time to get your money. You can get your refund faster by setting up direct deposit with your school. You can then use the funds for other costs approved by your grant — some examples are detailed below.

    If you have questions about your grant money, contact your college’s financial aid office.

By using grants to pay for your college education, you may be able to borrow less.

    Industry observers note that to maximize the grants you’re eligible to receive, enter accurate information on the FAFSA and complete it as soon as you can — some funds are first-come, first-served. Also, don’t limit yourself to federal or state grants — search and apply for as many privately funded grants as you can find.

You can use grant money on school and school-related expenses. Some grants may require you to meet eligibility requirements such as a minimum GPA or state residency. If you receive more grant money than your cost of attendance for a given school term, ask your financial aid office if you can put that grant money toward next year’s cost of attendance.

    By Alex Carchidi – Nov 25, 2026 at 1:37PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Anthropic ›.

    In a recent development, on Nov. 19, Anthropic (ANT +1.08%) became available to trade after raising a record $81.3 billion in its initial public offering (IPO), and just two days later, Bitcoin (BTC +0.80%) fell below its psychologically important $60,000 level to hit $55,130, its lowest since September 2024. For many investors, those events are connected, and Anthropic's debut is blamed for Bitcoin's poor performance.

    In short, one prevailing theory on the topic indicates that legions of investors sold their crypto to buy shares of Anthropic, just as they seemed to be doing right before Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX +1.30%)—better known as SpaceX—had its IPO in June. But does this narrative really hold up to scrutiny?

    U.S. spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) and their capital flows are notable bellwethers for Bitcoin's price, as they indicate demand for Bitcoin in the traditional financial system.

    Sources indicate that those ETFs saw $1.9 billion in net outflows from Nov. 5 to 13, and then another $1.8 billion from Nov. 16 to 20. By Nov. 23, November's outflows had reached $4.7 billion, a fresh record.

    Analysts have been largely consistent in saying that the IPO-drain story is pretty unproven; 10x Research's Markus Thielen called the timing coincidental. Similarly, TDX Strategies' Dick Lo called the IPO one factor affecting Bitcoin, but not necessarily the primary one, and he pointed to hotter-than-expected inflation data and rising Treasury yields as more important causes. Outflows accelerated the week the offering closed on Nov. 20, and then continued through Nov. 23.

    Industry observers note that market turbulence has also been bad for Bitcoin recently. In the week ending Nov. 20, U.S. stocks had their worst weekly performance since April 2025, due in part to the Federal Reserve's meeting minutes showing widespread support for more rate hikes, which tend to be bad for risky assets like cryptocurrencies. With Anthropic's stock now sinking, interest rates and economic uncertainty appear to be the bigger culprits.

    Bitcoin's performance after the SpaceX IPO in June is a helpful data point for deciding whether to buy the dip here.

    It has been revealed that spot Bitcoin ETFs saw a then-record $4.5 billion in net outflows that month, partly because the SpaceX IPO pulled capital away from crypto. Then, in July, they took in $403 million as the coin rose by 7.3%.

    So money returned to Bitcoin, but only in a trickle, which coincided with a decent price rebound. The same could well happen once the market's attention turns away from Anthropic, potentially within the next few weeks.

    Of course, one recent precedent isn't the same as a pattern.

    In a recent development, nothing about this IPO changes why people hold Bitcoin, so it still makes sense to buy slowly, in small amounts. Just be aware that if the Fed hikes interest rates further, it could be a long time before your Bitcoin purchases break even, and there could be a bit more downside in the near term.

    • The average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage ticked down to 7.05% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow.
    • Inflation data out this morning looks, at first glance, like bad news for mortgage rates.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Mortgage rates are a little lower this morning, and where they'll go next isn't totally clear.

    The average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage ticked down to 7.05% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is eight basis points lower than yesterday and 33 basis points lower than a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.).

    Inflation data out this morning looks, at first glance, like bad news for mortgage rates. But depending on how markets react, we could actually see lower mortgage rates. Keep reading after the charts for all the details.

    Below are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for perspective.

    In a recent development, P.S. Markets will be closed tomorrow for Thanksgiving, and Black Friday's a half day, and mortgage rates don't move much when the markets aren't moving. I won't be here to talk to you about mortgage rates, either, 'cause NerdWallet gives us Thursday and Friday off. Happy Thanksgiving!

    » Take the next step: Compare mortgage rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

    It has been revealed that mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to latest inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

    Like I mentioned above, it's not totally obvious where mortgage rates will head next. Let's walk through the two scenarios.

    Here's why rates could go up: This morning, we got October's Personal Consumption Expenditures price index, also known as PCE. It's the last measure of inflation to come out each month, but it's also the Federal Reserve's preferred metric, so PCE gets a lot of attention.

    Industry observers note that the stats came in mostly as predicted, though it's not like the predictions were good — inflation's been overly strong for a while. But the core year-over-year figure, which came in a tenth of a percent over predictions, could prove troublesome. Core PCE removes categories that can be extra volatile, so it's considered a measure that shows the underlying trend. In this case, the underlying trend is Not Good.

    It's already pretty much a lock that we'll see a rate hike at the Federal Reserve's December meeting, because yes, raising the federal funds rate is the Fed's main tool for taming inflation. The Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, but a rate-hiking cycle from the central bankers definitely keeps upward pressure on borrowing costs.

    In a recent development, on the other hand, here's why that same inflation data could help rates go down: Over the past several days, we've watched the stock market go on a wild ride, with the Anthropic IPO and the return of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Yesterday, things weren't looking good for tech stocks, and these inflation numbers could make it even worse.

    Recent findings suggest that the amount that tech companies have borrowed to fund AI buildout is a significant concern for investors, since companies will have to cover those costs before investors see any profits. It's already a substantial task, and if everything costs more thanks to inflation, it's that much harder.

    Sources indicate that this AI-related anxiety is rough on the stock market, but it's been a boon for Treasury bonds. More demand for bonds pushes up bond prices, which brings down bond yields (basically, the return investors get on a bond). Mortgage rates for 30-year loans are generally benchmarked to the yield on the 10-year Treasury note, so here's why you care about all of this: Lower Treasury yields means lower mortgage rates, too. If investors keep stressing about inflation eating into tech profits, we could see mortgage rates continue to move lower.

    That was a lot of info on inflation, but inflation's not the only major metric influencing rates.

    According to recent reports, let's back up for a second. The Federal Reserve tries to keep the economy steady by focusing on two key goals, often referred to as the Fed's dual mandate. One side is price stability — keeping inflation reasonable. The other is maximum employment, meaning those who want to work are able to find jobs.

    Next week we'll shift our focus to the employment side of the Federal Reserve's mandate, because the first week of the month is always all about employment data. On Tuesday, Dec. 1, we'll kick things off with the Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey (JOLTS). JOLTS can tip us off to trends in the labor market; stuff like whether folks are leaving jobs voluntarily or if companies have openings that are going unfilled.

    Industry observers note that on Wednesday, payroll firm ADP will release its monthly employment stats. ADP is looking at its own payroll data to get an idea of how the job market is growing or contracting. The numbers don't include the public sector, but ADP often provides a preview of how the jobs report will go.

    In a recent development, the Employment Situation Summary, better known as the jobs report, drops on Friday. This is the massive one, since it tells us the nation's unemployment rate. The jobs report's other major stat is, similar to ADP, how many jobs the economy added or lost in the previous month. Unlike ADP though, the jobs report is inclusive of everybody in the public and private sectors.

    Sources indicate that lately the labor market's been looking super healthy, which is great news for the economy but less positive for mortgage rates. When hiring's strong, the Fed can feel safer raising the federal funds rate (that's the short-term borrowing rate the central bankers adjust). Higher rates tend to discourage businesses from borrowing and expanding, so if the job market's on shaky footing, the central bankers are going to be cautious about raising the benchmark rate.

    What we're seeing now though, where inflation is clearly the problem and employment's just fine, is a recipe for higher rates. Again, the Fed doesn't control mortgage rates, but the central bank being in rate-hike mode puts upward pressure on mortgage rates.

    If we were to see employment falter in this latest round of numbers, it still probably wouldn't change the Fed's initiative. That would be one poor month for the labor market versus months upon months of inflation running rampant — so yeah, they'll keep an eye on jobs, but inflation's still the scourge.

    Our most likely source of lower mortgage rates in the short term is what I described above; investors who are leery of inflation and the promise of AI looking to the safe harbor of the bond market.

    » Learn more: How the Fed affects mortgage rates.

    Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you proposal to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

    With rates where they are right now, you could start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.55% or higher — but there just aren't too many people for whom that's true.

    Also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

    There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.

    Recent findings suggest that if the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

    Sources indicate that nerdWallet’s affordability calculator can help you estimate your potential monthly payment. If a new home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. Not only will this free up more cash flow for a future mortgage payment, it can also get you a better interest rate when you’re ready to buy.

    Sources indicate that if you already have a quote you’re happy with, you should consider locking your mortgage rate, especially if your lender offers a float-down option. A float-down lets you take advantage of a better rate if the market drops during your lock period.

    Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.

Management reported that Southeast Asia and East Asia remained resilient, whereas the North American market requires strategic adjustments to menu pricing and guest engagement to reach mainstream local diners. The company continues to advance its multi-brand strategy through the Pomegranate Strategy and is leveraging digital tools to refine its loyalty program, which currently contributes 90% of restaurant revenue.

With us today are Mr. Yu Li, Executive Director and CEO; and Ms. Lu Li, Chief Financial Officer and Joint Company Secretary.
